#189089. Tech Report: Darkest Dungeon 2's next bit of DLC is a short run, combat focused gauntlet where you must do everything in your power to please the audience

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (349 w)

Tech Report: Darkest Dungeon 2's next bit of DLC is a short run, combat focused gauntlet where you must do everything in your power to please the audience

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (349 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some new DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel.
  • It's called The Butcher's Asylum, as pleasant a name as any other, and it's a "stand alone gladiatorial arena game mode," that's due for release sometime in 2027.
  • This DLC isn't veering too far away from its roguelite origins, as it is still run-based, just on the shorter side and focusing more on the combat system.

The original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some new DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel. No, in fact the next bit of DLC for Darkest Dungeon 2 was teased only a couple of weeks ago, with a new trailer shared today actually showing off what it's all about.

It's called The Butcher's Asylum, as pleasant a name as any other, and it's a "stand alone gladiatorial arena game mode," that's due for release sometime in 2027. "The long-silent bells of the remote Asylum ring once more - souring the valley below with discordant and unsettling vibrations," the DLC's Steam page describes. "Garish heraldry, hastily stitched by unskilled hands, festoons the hilltop. Deep within the crumbling masonry of the Asylum, frenzied inmates compete in merciless bloodsport with monsters corralled the kingdom over. And to the victors of these debauched contests, the Butcher’s favour: a cure for their madness.".

This DLC isn't veering too far away from its roguelite origins, as it is still run-based, just on the shorter side and focusing more on the combat system. On your runs you'll need to prepare for the fights ahead, come across "insane enemy combinations never before possible," and spin a fun wheel which nets you prizes like newly introduced battle modifiers, charms and jinxes. There's also a new crowd meter, "a unique feature to the Asylum, can grant powerful effects to your team if you cater to the Crowd's demands. Failing to do so will only earn their scorn which raises the stakes and puts your success in jeopardy!".

The Butcher's Asylum also introduces a fresh playable character, The Ringmaster. You pick her up by winning bouts in the arena, and then you can recruit her in any game mode. She also serves as the narrator for the DLC, likely because of the passing of the main game's narrator Wayne June; Red Hook made clear earlier this year that they would never use generative AI to recreate June's voice, so I'm glad to see they haven't backstracked here.

Tech Report: Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (779 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let consumers scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Google indicates it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for consumers whose data was found on the dark web.
  • Industry observers note that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let owners run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let consumers scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the company discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with upcoming scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Google indicates it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for consumers whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a upcoming service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Industry observers note that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let owners run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google introduced the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One owners, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

Industry observers note that you'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

It’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

But perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that owners want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the company hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

It has been revealed that many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

It has been revealed that there isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

It has been revealed that if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

Finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar is reportedly looking to adapt Red Dead Redemption for the major and small screens.

According to The Ankler, Rockstar has been "throwing around a purchase price of more than $100 million minimum for licensing rights" to the Red Dead Redemption franchise with the hopes of making a movie or a TV show.

In Red Dead Redemption, the player controls a former outlaw named John Marston whose wife and son are held hostage by the government in exchange for Marston's bounty hunter services. It's an open-world game that's set in the year 1911 and has some horror elements (and some weird things happen when you let the game idle for a bit, depending on what you're doing in that moment). Red Dead Redemption 2, a prequel to the first game, was released in 2018.

Sources indicate that A Red Dead movie has been in demand for quite some time, dating all the way back to its 2010 release (with Brad Pitt initially tapped by fans as the perfect John Marston). Jack Black even noted that Red Dead had a "better story than The Last of Us" and therefore deserved its own live-action adaptation.

In a recent development, given that Far Cry, God of War, and Assassin's Creed are all in the works, and the fact that The Last of Us received some Emmy nominations... I'd say now is as good a time as any to turn your blockbuster video game into a live-action something or other.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here is an incredibly far-off release date you can pencil in (and then probably rub out because it'll be delayed again): the wild and wacky Showa American Story is coming to PS5 on 28th October 2027.

It was originally planned to launch in 2026, so this is a pretty substantial delay to the game, but the "core game content" is now complete, according to the developer.

The next 11 months will be dedicated to "polishing and optimizing the experience so that when you step into Showa American Story, it feels cohesive, responsive, and complete".

For those who don't know, Showa American Story is based on the scenario where "Japan has bought out most of the United States with its strong economic power. A surge of immigration has firmly planted Japanese culture within the American continent. Two cultures are rapidly amalgamated, although conflicts are inevitable, citizens gradually adapt to a life never imagined as time goes by.".

In a recent development, this leads to a bizarre adventure, which we got a small taste of at Gamescom earlier this year. You play Chigusa Choko, a female movie star brought back from the dead who sets out on a quest with vibes of Shenmue, Yakuza, and No More Heroes.

According to recent reports, what we played was incredibly unfinished and janky, but there was still some promise on show. Let's hope almost a year of polish and further work on the game turns it into a strong experience.

Can you wait that long to play Showa American Story? Let us know in the comments below.

60 hours in GTA 6 has me yearning for an online Leonida

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I honestly can't recall the last time I took such delight in existing within a virtual world as the way I have with Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida.
  • Pockets of culture erupt all over: the sheer redneckery of Port Gellhorn, the Latin culture that permeates Little Cuba, and the affluent snootiness of Capri that has cops flinging microaggressions in every direction.
  • It has been revealed that it's a world that, when I first ventured into it, I had no interest in exploring in a multiplayer setting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I honestly can't recall the last time I took such delight in existing within a virtual world as the way I have with Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida. Rockstar has delivered on its promise of both breadth and depth—the map is huge, but utterly stuffed with detail. Large, open highways shrink into single lanes surrounded by construction that force me to slam the brakes. Sidewalks sparse with pedestrians eventually lead to densely packed retail areas, restaurants, and clubs.

Pockets of culture erupt all over: the sheer redneckery of Port Gellhorn, the Latin culture that permeates Little Cuba, and the affluent snootiness of Capri that has cops flinging microaggressions in every direction. You don't need to undertake any missions in these areas to understand the people that live here—Rockstar has nailed so much of the environmental storytelling and the conversations between NPCs you'll stumble on as you roam.

It has been revealed that it's a world that, when I first ventured into it, I had no interest in exploring in a multiplayer setting. I spent an ungodly amount of time in GTA 5's Online mode when it first released. I was there on the ground for its incredibly shaky launch (I made a character and then got stuck in that birdseye view loading screen for hours, incredible stuff) and continued to sink time into it over the years, particularly during Covid.

Sources indicate that and I like it well enough, but its novelty has waned over the last decade. Its core experience is inherently different from what singleplayer brings, and I had yearned to return to a world less about blowing other players up with flying motorbikes and more about, well, blowing non-players up with regular motorbikes.

It has been revealed that but after 60 hours roaming around Leonida and witnessing what it has to offer? I now want nothing more than for Rockstar to spin this map into the next generation of Online. Even outside of missions and driving around, there are so many little things that I would kill to do with pals.

Grab a pack of brewskis from the convenience store, hop in a boat, and go fishing. Throw on our best all-American attire and get down and dirty in some mud racing. Seek out other players meticulously planning a jewellery store hold-up, only to swoop in and steal the goods for ourselves. Hit up the gym for a little workout before nipping to a nearby restaurant for a bite to eat. Leonida is a place that is so rife with things to do, and I can imagine doing almost all of them with some buddies by my side.

In a recent development, it's also the perfect opportunity for Rockstar to introduce things that are sorely missing for me right now. A lack of safehouses makes sense with GTA 6's offline story, but I yearn to buy highrise apartments and suburban houses. Maybe even buy a business or two, for a little side cash. There's also the matter of that gigantic casino and the go-kart track that are currently inaccessible but the latter of which is donning a large "COMING SOON" sign. It feels like I'm being taunted. Surely you wouldn't put these things in the game with no intention of opening them at some point… right?

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

According to recent reports, and even as someone who was never interested in nor dabbled with GTA Online's flourishing roleplaying scene, I've encountered so many instances where I've thought roleplaying in Leonida actually be pretty darn neat. I could become a RydeMe driver, or a Snapmatic influencer, or a backwater recluse who lives off the land. And when the game comes to PC? The potential for bending the world to account for even more professions becomes all the greater.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar hasn't actually noted a damn thing about GTA 6 Online right now, but it feels inevitable. Leonida is the biggest playground the developer has given players to date, and unleashing players across its sprawling map is Online's natural evolution. And, y'know, considering how much money GTAO has made over the last 13 years, I'm almost certain that Rockstar won't leave that kind of opportunity on the table.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chris Columbus directed Home Alone, but he came remarkably close to spending Christmas with the Griswolds instead.
  • In a recent development, onWildmen, the podcast hosted by Dylan Sprouse and the director's son Brendan Columbus, he revisited the feud that's been part of Hollywood lore for years.
  • I did not get along with Chevy Chase, and at this point famously now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chris Columbus directed Home Alone, but he came remarkably close to spending Christmas with the Griswolds instead. Before that movie became a holiday staple, he was supposed to direct National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation. Then he met Chevy Chase, and Columbus' latest account makes his decision to walk away sound even gutsier than I realized.

In a recent development, onWildmen, the podcast hosted by Dylan Sprouse and the director's son Brendan Columbus, he revisited the feud that's been part of Hollywood lore for years. I've heard the basic story before. What caught my attention was how badly he needed that movie, and how carefully he now talks about Chase. Columbus didn't dance around the history when the conversation turned to his early directing career:.

I did not get along with Chevy Chase, and at this point famously now.

In a recent development, columbus was coming off 1988's Heartbreak Hotel, which left him convinced his directing career might be over. He'd returned to Chicago and was staying with his in-laws when John Hughes called. The Christmas Vacation offer was supposed to get him back behind the camera, and he'd already started shooting second-unit footage.

In a recent development, the filmmaker has spoken harshly about Chase before. But this time, he said he's less interested in adding to the actor's bad press. Then he recalled how things reached the point where he called Hughes and quit:.

I’ve reached a point where I disliked him so much, and had so much anger toward him, I think I’ve become mature enough, and I think he’s taken so much shit in the press for the past five years that I’m sort of like I’m tired — I don’t wanna say he’s a bad person. So, basically, because I didn’t get along with Chevy, I had to tell John Hughes. I mentioned, ‘I can’t do the movie.' And I needed the movie desperately. I had already shot second unit on the movie for Christmas stuff in Chicago.

It has been revealed that I appreciate that Columbus is making room for a little perspective here. He didn't suddenly declare the feud resolved or pretend the experience was pleasant. He just sounds tired of spending another interview beating up Chase. Fair enough. I'd be tired of telling that story, too, especially knowing it started with a job he desperately needed. But the Harry Potter franchise filmmaker continued:.

Recent findings suggest that two weeks later, John sends me Home Alone. He notes, ‘Okay, you can't direct Christmas Vacation. I got this other script.’.

Jeremiah S. Chechik took over Christmas Vacation, and Home Alone arrived in theaters in 1990. I'm grateful both movies became Christmas classics, although it's amusing to imagine what Columbus might have done with Clark Griswold's disastrous holiday lighting display. Given those early meetings, I suspect he'd rather not imagine it at all.

Recent findings suggest that hearing Columbus discuss the timing makes it even stranger. A decision that could have ended his directing career led him to Kevin McCallister, Joe Pesci, and one of the most rewatchable Christmas movies around. I think I'm going to look at the opening credits a little differently this year. Excuse me while I go rewatch Home Alone for the 100th time with my Disney+ subscription.

Google has given its AI-powered "Ask Maps" feature a major upgrade, adding tools for trip planning, real-time route guidance, appointment finding, and saved-list search. The updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS.

Industry observers note that google rolled out Ask Maps last March as an AI assistant designed to handle questions and requests more complicated than simply searching the word "bar" or "groceries." Instead of performing simple keyword searches, the idea behind Ask Maps is that you can describe several specific requirements at once, and Maps will find places that match them all. For example, you could ask for a restaurant with outdoor seating for a certain number of people, and "Ask Maps" will factor in your past searches and give you results. Of course, AI assistants have a habit of making things up, so even with today's roll-out, you'll want to double-check your sources before you drive an hour to the wrong restaurant.

Sources indicate that to me, this is the most useful newly introduced feature launching today. Whether you're planning a day trip for holiday shopping or something more ambitious, like a three-day road trip with coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Ask Maps will put together a day-by-day schedule. Each initiative includes insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop, so you can see the whole route at a glance. Once you're happy with the plan, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

It has been revealed that when it's time to head out, you can ask Maps to pull up your itinerary, or look for the "itinerary" badge in your chat history. You'll see real-time details such as live traffic conditions, whether a place is currently open, and even the vibe at your next stop.

In a recent development, aims can change on the fly, too. Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or a lunch spot along the way, then tap to get directions to your next stop straight from the itinerary.

Here's what else you can use Ask Maps to do, starting today.

Recent findings suggest that pulling up directions now surfaces "Know Before You Go" tips for your route. These include where to park or charge your car, along with real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

Ask Maps is also gaining some agentic capabilities. Allegedly, you can just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses. In addition to finding appointments, Google notes this agent will be able to call local businesses on your behalf—stay tuned while I wait for the upgrade and test this one out myself.

If you keep lists of saved places, Ask Maps can now search them for you. Ask something like, "Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 5 in the next 30 minutes?" Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability, so you can pick a place and go.

These updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Travel itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know Before You Go" route tips and appointment finding are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.

It has been revealed that toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person. It was probably a wise choice on his part, obfuscating his current appearance with everyone's favourite annoying dog, essentially never speaking aloud in livestreams and instead using a text-to-speech bot, and posting only when there's notable enough Deltarune updates of if it would be very funny. But as it turns out, that sense of mystery extends to the team that's making Deltarune too, as Fox won't tell his devs how the game ends until they've built enough of it.

Earlier this week, the fall edition of the Deltarune newsletter went out, offering a brief update on the game's next and sixth chapter. That one's apparently now a "structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end," but that doesn't mean it's quite ready for release, as "some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation." I'd expect a 2027 release for this chapter, which is going to be a shorter one too.

But in typical tricky Tony fashion, there's an patch for chapter seven where he makes it sound like no one but him knows how the whole game is going to end. "Well, we've only just started…," he explains of the progress. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.".

In a recent development, I'm glad they all think it's fun, the wait for me personally certainly ain't. I do wonder if this speaks to a certain anxiety over how the game will shape up. Following the release of chapter five I was subjected to all manner of theories about what's to come by my partner gorging on YouTube videos from folks who mostly just seem quite excited about it all, even if a lot of them sound wrong. So I imagine there must be a little bit of weight to all of those varying expectations.

Fox did note in the newsletter that "unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!" so perhaps I'm speaking a load of hogwash! That said, I'm furious that a character called Apple Girlington didn't make it into chapter five, so you can expect to hear from my lawyers, Mr. Fox.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're having trouble heisting the GTA 6 Schafter v12 for Raul, it's easier than you might think. The problem is that you've gotten used to stealing cars for Moses in GTA 6 Chapter 1, but now you're working for Raul, and his jobs are a little more... unusual. So, if you're driving away from the scene of the crime in a hot new motor, police on your tail, wondering why you're being told your job's not done, here's where you might be going wrong when trying to steal the Schafter v12 in GTA 6.

If you're struggling with this mission, the problem is most likely that you're stealing the wrong car. You should be looking for the shabby green car parked under the canopy with its trunk roof missing.

Industry observers note that having been keeping an eye out for so many nice cars by this point, be it for yourself, for Moses, or for Raul, you're lulled into a false sense of security. You go into this mission all guns blazing, literally, thinking you know what's up and that you don't need to waste time Wainking it. That stunning muscle car with the growling exposed engine and massive exhausts must be the car you're after, right? Wrong. Clearly placed here to lead you astray on purpose, that's actually the strangely reasonably priced Imponte Bloodbath Phoenix, so I recommend heading back to the area and taking that one for yourself later. For the Car Service mission, however, you'll need to drive away in the crumbling Benefactor Shafter v12.

Other than that, the only trouble you'll meet with this mission is the same as ever: a few criminals with weapons ready to be drawn. The best way to complete this one is to head onto the roof from round the back of the gated area before taking them all out with a silenced handgun, which I recommend for most small-to-medium heists at this stage.

Recent findings suggest that if you're looking for more cars to steal for yourself, make sure you pick up the Paul Walker GTA 6 car, inspired by the 1995 Fast and Furious Mitsubishi Eclipse. And don't skip over the pink Porsche in GTA 6, which you can only get if you pay attention in Chapter 2.

It has been revealed that edia has revealed Kendo Rage 1&2, a two-game collection featuring side-scrolling action game Kendo Rage and fighting game sequel Kendo Rage 2. It will launch for PlayStation 5, Switch, and PC via Steam on March 18, 2023.

Kendo Rage first rolled out for Suepr Famicom in January 1993 in Japan, followed by Super Nintendo Entertainment System in October 1993 in North America. The sequel, which never saw a localized release, launched for Super Famicom in March 1995 in Japan, followed by PlayStation in November 1995.

Industry observers note that in Japan, Kendo Rage 1&2 will be priced at 7,800 yen for the standard physical or digital edition (8,580 yen with tax), and 14,800 yen for the physical Special Edition (16,280 yen with tax). The latter includes a copy of the game, a replica poster-style large tapestry, a soundtrack CD, and a replica flyer set.

Industry observers note that it’s kind of hard to believe that Vanna White has been co-hosting Wheel of Fortune for nearly 45 years as of the 2026 television schedule. For thousands of episodes, White has been turning the iconic letter on the show, but her beginning was as humble as you would expect. In a recent appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, White told the story of her audition, why she was chosen by legendary producer Merv Griffin, and even what her first puzzle was (and the first letter she turned).

Of the audition process, White explained:.

It has been revealed that merv Griffin, God bless him. He chose me…. [There were] over 200 girls. And I noted to him, ‘Why did you choose me?’ He said, ‘You turn the letters better than anyone else.’.

I mean, yeah, fair enough, right? Though White’s role on the show has grown a lot over the years, far beyond only turning (now touching) the letters (and working hard for her salary). In those early days, that was the job. If you’re going to get the gig, you better be elegant when you are flipping those lit-up boxes around! No one can argue with Griffin’s logic, and almost five incredible decades later, it's clear he couldn’t have made a better choice.

Speaking of turning letters, Fallon follows up White’s story about getting the job on Wheel by asking her if she remembers her first puzzle, and despite thousands of puzzles since, she does:.

It was ‘General Hospital,’ and my first letter was a T.

Sources indicate that according to White, she’d wanted to be a TV star since she first saw her “uncle,” actor Christopher George, in an episode of his show The Rat Patrol in the mid ‘60s. George, it should be noted, was not a biological uncle, but was a close friend of her mother’s. On her first day filming, however, she was still quite nervous (and was even worried it wouldn't work out in the early days), telling Fallon:.

According to recent reports, I was so nervous. Oh my gosh. My teeth were [chattering], I couldn’t even talk. I was like, ‘Oh my gosh, is this really happening?’.

Recent findings suggest that famously, that wasn't the first time appearing on a game show. Two years before getting the job, she appeared as a contestant on The Price Is Right. Fallon and White talked about that appearance, which, sadly, ended without her making it on stage with Bob Barker, as she was never closest to the price of the item while on contestants' row.

It has been revealed that white's first episode of Wheel aired on December 13, 1982, which means we’re just a couple of weeks away from her 44th anniversary. Pat Sajak was her co-host, of course, and the duo would work together for the next 42 years before Sajak retired from the show in 2024. She continues to co-host with Ryan Seacrest and has shown no signs of slowing down as she approaches 70 years old.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even though Sony has paid god-only-knows how much money to market GTA 6 as a borderline PS5 exclusive, it turns out that Rockstar's magnum opus actually runs better on Xbox.
  • This is according to those tech wizards over at Digital Foundry, who have spent hours comparing the open world title across base PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though Sony has paid god-only-knows how much money to market GTA 6 as a borderline PS5 exclusive, it turns out that Rockstar's magnum opus actually runs better on Xbox.

This is according to those tech wizards over at Digital Foundry, who have spent hours comparing the open world title across base PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S.

Recent findings suggest that now, we already know that GTA 6 isn't perfect on the standard PS5. It suffers from minor but sometimes prolonged frame rate drops during busy scenes — whether you're speeding through heavy traffic or fighting for your life in a particularly explosive combat encounter.

In a recent development, but in a rather shocking twist, the Xbox Series X outdoes the PS5 in this department. While Digital Foundry's testing shows that the frame rate dips are still present on the Series X, they're nowhere near as frequent.

They write: "PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips.".

The article continues: "Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off.".

This isn't what you'd expect, given that every PlayStation-related GTA 6 advertisement and trailer has boasted that the game 'Plays Best on PS5'.

Okay, so that slogan might technically be true if we're counting the PS5 Pro, where GTA 6 does perform best by some distance, thanks to a combination of the console's PSSR upscaler and increased GPU power.

But on base hardware, it's Microsoft that wins out.

"Overall, the PS5 Pro leads the rankings with its superior visual detail and rock-solid 30fps target, followed by the Xbox Series X — which edges out the standard PS5 through better performance stability," Digital Foundry concludes.

In a recent development, are you surprised by these findings? Have you noticed any frequent frame rate drops in GTA 6 on PS5? Wonder if we'll ever see 60fps again in the comments section below.

Sharon Horgan had a string of British hits (including a couple we'll talk about here), before scoring stated successes with Divorce, Shining Vale, and Bad Sisters. She's quickly rising in the ranks of TV super-producers, the acerbically funny HBO Max rom-com Youth (in which she also stars) being just the latest.

This earlier series created by and starring Sharon Horgan is a family sitcom that feels far more believable than most, seeing Irish primary school teacher Sharon (Horgan) hooking up with American ad exec Rob (Rob Delaney) over the course of a week, only to discover that she's pregnant once he returns home. They don't really have feelings for each other, but decide to give it a go at being a couple, eventually falling into marriage just before the birth of their child. There are lots of jokes and plenty of acerbic dialogue, but this isn't Married... with Children. Sharon and Rob can be a bit nasty to each other and to their sloppy friend group, but there's also something rather sweet in the show's conviction that having someone to be a mess with can be one of life's great joys. Stream Catastrophe on Prime Video.

A little more of a high-concept here, but nevertheless an effective show about reimagining yourself in middle age. Younger follows Liza Miller (Sutton Foster), a recently divorced woman in her 40s who finds that age is a barrier to reentering the publishing industry she left years earlier. After a compliment convinces her that she could pass for a younger woman (poor thing), she manages to convince the right people that she's just 26 in order to land an entry-level job. Seven seasons of misadventures ensue, but much of the show revolves around the twisty-turny relationship between Liza and Josh (Nico Tortorella), a tattoo artist in his twenties. Stream Younger on Netflix.

Sources indicate that bridget Everett stars as Sam Miller, who struggles to find her latest direction after moving back to her hometown to care for her dying sister. (Don't worry: There's plenty of comedy in the drama, and it's not as heavy as it sounds.) She's solidly middle-aged and starting over, kinda—making new friends in a familiar environment where she has to confront the past and the future alike. Luckily, her love of singing—and a community of goofy oddballs—are there to help. It's another story of a person of a certain age, trying to rebuild their life following an upheaval. Stream Somebody Somewhere on HBO Max.

When all else fails: Start a punk band. This drama from Sally Wainwright (Gentleman Jack) sees five women start a punk band as a lark, just a fun way to kill some time by entering a local talent context. The women realize very promptly, though, that they're very, very pissed off—about the workplace for women, menopause, a diminished dating pool, caring for aging parents and grown children—all of it tied up in the ways in which we treat women, and particularly middle-aged women. The band is a way to reclaim their voices, which doesn't erase or negate any of their problems nor drama (and there's plenty here), but gives them a platform with which to make some noise about it. Stream Riot Women on Britbox.

More of a traditional sitcom, not that there's anything wrong with that, this one builds a lot of goodwill with the performance of Leanne Morgan, its lead and co-creator (alongside Susan McMartin and Chuck Lorre). She plays the show's lead: a Knoxville, Tennessee wife and mom, who finds herself suddenly single in her 50s after her husband of 33 years leaves her. It's a genial, old-school hang-out show with a phenomenal veteran supporting cast that includes Kristen Johnston, Ryan Stiles, and Tim Daly. Stream Leanne on Netflix.

Michele Buteau, who also co-created the series) stars here as a fashion-forward stylist who'd devoted herself to the wrong guy for way too long. As the series opens, Mavis Beaumont is ready for a fresh start, putting herself and her career first—which does not preclude falling into a number of romantic entanglements. As she says more than once, she's going to take on the fashion world with a "body-positive attitude, cute v-neck, and some lip-gloss." Stream Survival of the Thickest on Netflix.

Industry observers note that certainly the goofiest take here on the idea of starting over in mid-life, this is very much a traditional three-camera sitcom, albeit one with a stacked cast of TV legends. Writer Melanie (Valerie Bertinelli), beautician Joy (Jane Leeves), and soap diva Victoria (Wendie Malick) wind up spending a wild night in Cleveland after a plane to Paris is diverted, discovering in the process that, while they're seen as over-the-hill back in Los Angeles, they're all Ohio 10s—though the sassy caretaker of their house, Elka (Betty White), might not agree. Stream Hot in Cleveland on Paramount+.

She'a s hair younger than Alex, but Fleabag (she's only ever referred to as "Fleabag") is trying to rebuild her life after a bad breakup, with extremely mixed results. This very dark comedy-drama follows a free-spirited, deeply angry single young woman living in London and sharing her romantic ups and downs via confessional asides to us, the audience. She falls, rather reluctantly, for "The Priest" (Andrew Scott)—while she's a confirmed atheist, and he's obviously not, the show doesn't turn aside from the general messiness of the situation. Phoebe Waller-Bridge won separate Emmys as the star, creator, and writer of the series. Stream Fleabag on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that maisel was one of Prime’s first truly buzzy original series, a comedy-drama from Amy Sherman-Palladino (Gilmore Girls) about the title’s Midge Maisel (Rachel Brosnahan), a long-time Fresh York housewife of the late 1950s who discovers a talent for stand-up comedy. Inspired by the real-life careers of comedians like Totie Fields and Joan Rivers, the show is warm and welcoming, with great performances and dialogue; it also achieves something rare in being a show about comedy that’s actually funny. Stream The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel on Prime Video.

The big life change in this earlier Sharon Horgan hit is a little different: Julia Johnstone's mother had been a big help in taking care of Julia's children, but she's not going to do it anymore, leaving this working mom (Anna Maxwell Martin) to take the full brunt of childcare for the first time (her husband in the picture, but not much use). She joins up with other working moms involved with a local support group, including shallow Amanda (Lucy Punch), star of her own ongoing spin-off. Stream Motherland on Prime Video and Britbox.

Eldritch Empathy, then, seems like a grand ole game to satisfy my wanton need to experience such things. It's a puzzle roguelite that isn't exactly a Papers Please-like but certainly feels reminiscent of one, where you have to "analyse corrupted creatures, purify their emotions and learn how to communicate with an eldritch being.".

According to recent reports, you kick things off by embodying Eike, a "young woman who has strange dreams and sightings of twisted creatures in the woodlands neighbouring the sleepy Swiss village she lives in." She decides to investigate these mysterious circumstances herself, where she comes upon these corrupted critters in the woods. You need to thoroughly inspect them, using a book to determine what is going on with them and what they need exactly; it's akin to checking the passport rulebook in Papers Please, hence the comparison.

After figuring out what's going on with these creatures, you then "use and transform symbols to create paths through the creatures' insides. You may use care and precision to navigate to the correct corrupted emotion you have identified from your investigation and purify it. You may also use your tools to cause harm. Whatever you choose, your actions will have consequences." Ominous! You can also proposal your runs ahead of time, heading down paths that may offer you some boons here and there, like the option to restore a bit of sanity (it's one of those Lovecraftian kind of horror games, as loathe as I am that we still have to reference that guy).

According to recent reports, also be wary of the fact that actions you take out in the woods can affect your home and community. It's a roguelite with consequences! Mwahahha! Looks pretty neat overall, and has some tasty pixel art attached to it too. No release date just yet, but I'd assume it'll arrive no earlier than next year. You can wishlist it right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The buzziest film on the 2026 movie schedule has to be You Can See Everything, and it just hit a major milestone by crossing the $100 million mark at the box office. For a movie that was made for a reported $7 million, it’s certainly one of the most successful A24 releases ever, but the Elizabeth Holmes documentary is nowhere close to the top-grossing documentary of all time, worldwide. That record belongs to the King of Pop himself for the posthumously released Michael Jackson: This Is It from 2009. How does it stack up to other documentaries? Well, it depends on how you count things.

Anyway you count, in terms of worldwide gross, This Is It sits at the top of the list, with almost $268 million, according to Box Office Mojo. Second on the list is Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour, which made $261 million worldwide, and most of it ($180 million) in the United States. Both far outpace Fahrenheit 9/11, which is third on the list and the first non-music documentary. The Michael Moore-directed movie about the lead-up to the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq was a box office sensation from the moment it was released.

You Can See Everything wasn’t quite the rocket ship that Fahrenheit 9/11 was out of the box, but it did a ton of steady business for weeks, finally topping the weekend box office in its third week of release. Now, after its release in the United Kingdom, the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim-directed documentary has joined rarefied air as a documentary hitting that milestone. The $100 million mark slots You Can See Everyone into 7th worldwide.

Recent findings suggest that nature documentaries litter the top ten, with the IMAX-exclusive Everest, (filmed during the disastrous season on the mountain in 1996) coming in fourth all time, Earth coming in at #6 on the list (Penguins is 5th), and Oceans is 9th. The other slots in the top ten are both music-related: Justin Bieber: Never Say Never (8th) and One Direction: This Is Us (10th).

Here are the top ten-grossing documentaries of all time (worldwide), along with their gross, according to Box Office Mojo:.

That means the only two non-music and non-nature documentaries in the top ten are Fahrenheit 9/11 and You Can See Everything. It also means that You Can See Everything won’t be catching up to Michael Jackson. I don’t expect You Can See Everything to improve significantly at the worldwide box office. Elizabeth Holmes may be fascinating and infamous here, but Jackson was a massive star in every corner of the globe. In fact, domestically, This Is It actually trails You Can See Everything by almost $20 million.

Industry observers note that it’s the domestic numbers that really tell you the story of just how buzzy the film is, as it ranks 3rd all time at U.S. box offices, behind Fahrenheit 9/11 and The Eras Tour. It also has a very good chance of separating itself from the pack as the first documentary nominated for Best Picture at the Oscars, something not even March of the Penguins did. Who knows, maybe it will be competing against this year's Michael in that category.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are currently being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

Recent findings suggest that the investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

The appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

In a recent development, looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over ten years ago and half-a-decade before Elden Ring, FromSoftware head Hidetaka Miyazaki stated he felt unworthy of comparisons to Zelda.

In a recent development, speaking to Rolling Stone in 2016 (via Wayback Machine), Miyazaki was asked about comments that the Souls titles – and Bloodborne – are what The Legend of Zelda series should've evolved into. The developer responded at the time, "When I was a student, The Legend of Zelda was truly monumental, so to be perfectly honest, I feel deeply unworthy of the comparison.".

According to recent reports, hidetaka Miyazaki au sujet de Zelda : "Quand j'étais étudiant, The Legend of Zelda était vraiment monumental, tellement que pour être honnête, je me sens profondément indigne de cette comparaison. The legend of Zelda et Dark Souls sont des jeux différents appartenant à des genres différents et ils sont guidés par différents concepts de game design. Ils n'aspirent pas aux mêmes idéaux. Et s'il y a des similitudes, c'est probablement parce que The Legend of Zelda est devenu avec le temps une sorte de manuel pour les jeux d'action 3D" Source : Rolling Stones, traduction NintendoMasterNovember 23, 2026.

According to recent reports, and while Zelda was definitely an influence on Miyazaki's work, he somewhat rebuked the comparison, saying, "The Legend of Zelda and Dark Souls are different games belonging to different genres though, and they're guided by different concepts of game design. They don't need to aspire to the same ideals." He adds, "If there are similarities, they probably stem from the fact that The Legend of Zelda became a sort of textbook for 3D action games," specifically in reference to Ocarina of Time.

In a recent development, of course, we're in a far different world than we were 10 years ago – both with games and outside of them. Namely, The Legend of Zelda would reinvent itself with the release of Breath of the Wild months later, becoming one of the most acclaimed games ever made. And then five years after that, Miyazaki would take inspiration from Breath of the Wild while directing Elden Ring, which would also go on to be a generation-defining game like Zelda before it, and subsequently the developer's most successful game ever.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sits before Elden Ring and Skyrim as the 26th best game of all time, according to Metacritic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek appears to have followed through on their threat to release the executable of the Xbox build of GTA 6 they put into the wild last week, calling it "an early Christmas gift" for followers and explicitly linking the leak to efforts to recreate the game on PC: "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects.".

Cyberleek released a near-complete build of GTA 6 late last week, holding back only the main exe—the part that makes everything else run, basically—until either their crypto coin achieved a $15 million market cap, or November 23, whichever came first. The crypto missed badly, but time marches on, and so here we are.

According to recent reports, the release of the exe, naturally, includes a call for more "donations" in its readme file (via Reddit) which Cyberleek said will go toward a secretive project "for the gamers." They also taunted Take-Two Interactive's efforts to track them down: "Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has.".

Industry observers note that leaks in the game industry aren't anything fresh, but this case is unique: GTA 6, effectively the biggest videogame of all time, still hasn't been announced for PC, as is Take-Two's way. But the advent of AI means the game could be emulated on our platform far more quickly than was possible in the past—some modders estimated it could happen within a week.

One of the leads on the Leonida recomp project predicted that things will start to move promptly from here:.

At the same time, Shayder tempered expectations in a message on the Leonida Discord, saying "it will take at least a week" for the project to reach the point where GTA will be playable on PC.

How that unofficial emulated made-with-AI build would compare to the real deal is an open question, and I strongly suspect the answer will be "not well," but even just having something GTA 6-ish playable on PC is a headache that I'm pretty sure Take-Two would rather not have to deal with. I also wonder whether it will prompt Take-Two to release GTA 6 on PC more swiftly than it has with previous releases. A rumor to that effect surfaced in October and I had serious doubts, but it's possible that ongoing emulation efforts will expedite its arrival..

It has been revealed that I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own reveals through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.

Sources indicate that NIGHTEYE.TV is a strange little place. I call it a place, it's a fake TV floating in a Unity default texture void, lending it a Backroomsian vibe, but even if there's not much there to ground yourself in, the goggle box is enticing all the same. It beckons you to turn it on, a series of buttons all linking to different "channels." What awaits you isn't television, however. Instead you'll find games, mostly of the weirdo, freako, sicko variety, rapidly setting the tone.

🌕NIGHT EYE TV’s initial form is live!🌑 Check out the site and follow our Indiegogo campaign at www.nighteye.tv![image or embed].

Industry observers note that in its current incarnation, it's mostly just a collection of clips of these various art games, with direct links to them hidden away in a menu, but a good collection it is. You'll find Nathalie Lawhead's Everything is Going to Be OK, Jeremy Couillard's more recent Soul Injector Commando, and Taylor McCue's He Fucked The Girl Out Of Me. Some clips are longer than others, acting as sort of segments of playthroughs, but it all feels like an exciting evolution of what public-access television was.

The ultimate goal is for it to be a curated platform where you can buy a rotating selection of games. Most of the sale goes back to the original artist, and 15% gets put into a community pool to be split amongst all of the contributors, with the last 15% going towards keeping everything running. As it stands, that's not quite ready yet. You can help make it happen, though, as right now an Indiegogo campaign is running to help it all get fully operational. Worth chucking a few quid I reckon!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the tech giant which has long played a major role in PC gaming.

According to recent reports, following Huang's departure, The Upcoming York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

The report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, said everyone hoped they'd drop dead.

Huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".

It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's mentioned often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.

Sources indicate that A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the Latest York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, mentioned the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".

Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly stated earlier this week that the tech giant "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, that's now changing.
  • According to recent reports, as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices. You can send voice messages, photos, and videos that will "self-destruct" after they're opened, limiting (if not eliminating) the risk of your friends keeping them forever. However, View Once has a major limitation: While WhatsApp will let you send voice memos and images that way, you can't use it to send texts, meaning every one you send will live on (unless you unsend it yourself).

According to recent reports, that's now changing. As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too. Soon enough, you'll be able to send voice memos, photos, videos, and texts as one-time-only messages. That way, you can send sensitive information via text—say, a password or an important account number—without worrying about it persisting. Here's how it works: You craft your text message as you usually do, but rather than tap the send button, you hold it. You'll see the usual "Schedule message" option, but once the feature rolls out, you'll also find a upcoming "View Once" option as well.

According to recent reports, as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it. WhatsApp also explains that recipients cannot share, forward, save, or take screenshots of View Once text messages. Recipients won't see the text appear in the usual chat interface, either; instead, your recipient will need to open the message in a separate window. Once they close this page, the message disappears.

As mentioned above, this feature is currently in testing, so it's only available to WhatsApp beta testers. What's more, only the Android version of the beta has access at the moment, so iOS beta testers are out of luck. (That stated, the WhatsApp iOS beta is perpetually full, so there's not much you could do even if WhatsApp made this test available on iPhone.).

It has been revealed that if you have an Android device, you can enroll in the WhatsApp beta to try out "View Once" text messages today. According to WABetaInfo, the feature is live as of WhatsApp version 2.26.45.6. To enroll, open the WhatsApp beta page on the Google Play store and enroll your account in the beta. If you don't have WhatsApp on your phone already, download it here; if you do, reload the page and install the latest patch. This will update your existing WhatsApp app to the latest beta version.

A solo indie dev has made $1.3 million on Steam in one week with the release of their first game – a roguelike auto-battling defense title the dev openly admits they used generative AI throughout its entire development.

Recent findings suggest that say hello to Slotbound – a roguelike where players pull the lever on a slot machine to summon units and build an army, using items to manipulate the odds in their favor. It debuted on November 13 and has since accumulated 91% Very Positive reviews, with over 200,000 copies sold in six days.

In a recent development, obviously, a lot of sales means a lot of revenue, and developer Optima Arch took to Twitter last week to share just how successful their game has been. "My first game, Slotbound has made nearly $1.33 million in gross revenue in just its first week on Steam!" they write, sharing a screenshot of their earnings and player stats. "I've barely had time to process any of this between fixing bugs and pushing updates.

Recent findings suggest that "I started developing the game alone just over a year ago, and I honestly never imagined it would reach this point," they continue. "Thank you so much to everyone who's played and supported it. There's still plenty to improve, and I'll keep working hard to make it better!".

Industry observers note that my first game, Slotbound has made nearly $1.33 million in gross revenue in just its first week on Steam! I've barely had time to process any of this between fixing bugs and pushing updates😅 I started developing the game alone just over a year ago, and I honestly never imagined it would reach this point. Thank you so much to everyone who's played and supported it. There's still plenty to improve, and I'll keep working hard to make it better! #Slotbound #indiedevNovember 20, 2026.

This success comes despite the use of generative AI throughout Slotbound's development, which Optima Arch has been transparent about since well before release. In a July Reddit post, they describe it as an "AI-assisted game," noting that they "didn’t come from a traditional game development background" and so "decided to use AI tools to finally turn one of my game ideas into something real.".

According to recent reports, as far as the tech's utility goes, they noted at the time that "AI was involved throughout the project, especially with coding and parts of the visual workflow. But most of the process was still designing systems, testing builds, fixing bugs, reworking balance, removing ideas that weren’t fun, and rebuilding things until they felt right.".

It has been revealed that in the AI disclosure on Steam, Optima Arch indicates: "Various visual assets and promotional materials for Slotbound were created with the assistance of generative AI tools. All AI-generated content was reviewed, refined, and integrated by the developer to ensure consistency with the game's artistic direction and quality standards.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It has been revealed that AI usage in game development is always contentious – for many, the use of AI is enough to put them off from supporting something at all, and its utility is almost always met with major backlash. Crimson Desert developer Pearl Abyss found itself in hot water earlier this year when its huge open-world game launched with some AI-generated assets, for example – these were quickly patched out, but the controversy didn't stop the studio from outlining its looks to implement the tech "throughout our entire development pipeline" going forward.

In a recent development, more recently, Massive Walk devs faced backlash for previously undisclosed AI use in their co-op hit's development. So far, though, AI doesn't seem to be having a major negative impact on Slotbound's success.

Half of all games released on Steam will use AI by 2028, study predicts: "AI lowers the barrier not just to make a game but to make several.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that "I think the version of BioWare that survives EA better is a version where we drop down to one franchise at a time, maybe just one franchise at all. Maybe we just carve SWTOR off and they become an independent studio within EA, because I don't know how what I'm about to say makes sense if you don't do that. But you ship Mass Effect, you ship Dragon Age, and then one of those wins—I hate this—one of those wins and then you just become a one-project studio. There are lots of studios within EA that did that and it didn't work—they still got murdered in their sleep, so maybe that doesn't work anyway." Via an interview with Pembridge.

Many are asking themselves how a legendary studio like BioWare, which is responsible for staples of the PC gaming genre like Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and the OG Baldur's Gate, alongside Mass Effect and Dragon Age, can be shuttered.

Recent findings suggest that former Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah has already explained how the studio was backed into a corner by EA. Escalating financial pressure led to the poor decisions and subpar games we saw ahead of BioWare's closure. But what if it had all gone differently? Despite everything, Darrah does question whether there was a way for BioWare to survive under EA.

Sources indicate that "BioWare's entire existence under EA—it was essentially zero sum, if somebody was getting resources it was coming at the expense of somebody else," Darrah explains. "It's almost like BioWare has run exactly the same way for its entire existence. But the external constraints were different. So in the early days when BioWare needed more people it hired more people. That's like Baldur's Gate 1, Neverwinter Nights, in the early days when we have all these different threads and branches.

According to recent reports, "And then in 2007/2008, when the EA constraints come in, the same desires are there, we need more people to ship our games so the way we fix that in that time period is by cutting off all those other branches. So [Jade Empire sequel] Revolver goes away and the Handheld [Development] Group goes away … and so Dragon Age and Mass Effect eats everything.".

Sources indicate that the alternative? Scaling things down to meet EA's needs. "Budgets keep going up, but we're still not getting bigger… So what's happening is that the walls are closing in and we're trying to be three things [SWTOR, Mass Effect, Dragon Age] and arguably we can only afford to be two things, or one thing." There's no telling whether this would've saved BioWare, but it has worked for other studios.

"Maxis figured out how to live inside of EA and BioWare never did," Darrah adds. Focusing on just one project does seem to be the answer, or at least Darrah believes it has been for Maxis and Battlefield Studios, which both had games that initially underperformed and weren't well received. "If [Battlefield Studios] don't work on Battlefield then you might as well shut the studio down. So they all work on Battlefield 4 and they fix Battlefield 4 and it becomes successful, like very successful after the fact. The Sims 4, same thing.".

On the other hand "Mass Effect Andromeda ships and then Dragon Age 4 which has been starving for resources is like 'No, no [the devs] are supposed to come to us. Where are they?' That need to keep them in place isn't there in the same way. So when I say BioWare didn't adapt to EA, that's what I mean.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6. After accusing Rockstar Games of using his likeness without consent and then demanding a $10m payout, the two parties have seemingly settled their differences.

Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him. The former tattoo model, who first went viral because of a mugshot that shared an uncanny resemblance to Batman's Joker, soon called on Rockstar to pay him $2m. His demand swiftly shot up to $10m, before he dropped all legal threats and politely asked to officially work with the developer.

Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.

GTA 6 players wasted no time, and quickly found the suspect first teased way back in that original 2023 trailer. In its quest to parody all parts of modern life under capitalism, GTA 6 lets you doomscroll through a social media app called Snapmatic, which flings an endless number of short-form clips and thirst traps at you. If you're lucky enough, or if you scroll for long enough, you'll find a video of Sullivan's in-game counterpart beating up a fake lookalike. He certainly sounds like Sullivan, too.

"Two years y'all been talking crazy about me," he wrote under a recent Instagram post. "Who got the last laugh now?!".

According to recent reports, the GTA 6 credits were illuminating for other reasons, too. We finally know who voices the game's loveable duo, Jason and Lucia, for one. All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar workers also appear in GTA 6's credits. The controversial move eventually led to accusations of union busting on Rockstar's part, which is currently being investigated as part of an employment tribunal in Scotland.

#189059. I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1008 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1008 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better?
  • You'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up.
  • According to recent reports, proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—currently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better? Pangram is one of the leaders in the field, promising a "near-zero false positive rate" by looking at "subtle cues" in the writing, based on a training and feedback model comparing human-made content with the AI equivalent.

You'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up. After a short story was flagged by Pangram and then judged to be free from AI, the detection engine has been accused of bias against text from minority writers.

According to recent reports, proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—currently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written. So far, the reward is unclaimed.

As the AI detector has recently added AI image and video detection to its capabilities, it seemed a good time to put Pangram's analysis skills to the test for myself. Here's how it performed in the three different content types.

On the human side, I picked out 10 of my most recent articles for Lifehacker, known to be written by a person because I personally wrote them—in the traditional way, I fretted over word choices, went back and changed sentences, and accidentally left in a variety of typos that editors thankfully fixed.

For the AI content, I rotated between ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, and got the LLMs to write 10 articles with the same headlines and the same approximate number of words, for a tech-savvy audience. I even asked the AI apps to vary their language use, so that the output would "read less like an LLM has written it.".

Pangram's AI text detector lets you upload files, but to make the task a little harder, I copied and pasted all of the text into the online article, so it wouldn't be able to rely on any metadata included in the file. The scans got the correct result each and every time: Human-written text came back as 100% human, and AI-written text came back as 100% AI.

Industry observers note that what's more, Pangram was certain about its results. All of the human writing was marked as highly likely to be human, and the vast majority of the AI writing was marked as highly likely to have come from an LLM. There were only a handful of phrases or sentences across thousands of AI words that got a "medium" rather than a "high" ranking for AI.

Sources indicate that now, there have been some edge cases where Pangram has got it wrong—like a poem repeating the same six words thousands of times—but as far as this sample goes, it can't be faulted. Clearly, my writing is too idiosyncratic and too clunky to be confused for the smooth sheen of AI-produced prose.

It has been revealed that to be fair, I do have another advantage over AI: I can actually test out devices and apps in a way that LLM bots can't. ChatGPT can't experiment with One UI 9 (at least not yet), though it can scrape the web for various experiments and tests that real people have done.

In a recent development, however, I was able to fool Pangram to some extent by alternating AI paragraphs with human-written paragraphs. The text was flagged as AI, but the percentage estimate was typically lower (20-25%) than what it actually was (around 50%). If you're offloading some but not all of your writing to AI, some of it might slip though as real.

Image and video detection is the new string to Pangram's bow, so I sifted through my phone's photo and video library for some pieces of content to test the AI on. Again, I used copy and paste to get the files into Pangram rather than uploading them, to limit how much information the AI detector could get from metadata.

Recent findings suggest that again, all the human-made content was recognized as such, with a very high level of certainty—whether it was complicated crowd shots or simpler images of natural scenes. Presumably, there are even more signals to go off than there are with writing, including camera movements, colors, style, consistency, and composition.

Next up, I generated a few images and videos in Google Gemini and ChatGPT, requesting results that would look as photorealistic and "non-AI" as possible—the resulting files covered people, animals, and buildings. As before, I used copy, paste, and a few screengrabs to try and limit the metadata Pangram had access to.

Here, too, the AI identification was spot on, with all of the artificial content recognized as such, to a high level of confidence. This is perhaps not surprising: I think AI images and especially AI video still have more "tells" than AI writing, especially if you've seen a lot of it, so I wasn't expecting Pangram to fail here.

Industry observers note that I did try experimenting with real photos that had a little bit of AI in them, what with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT now so good at image editing, as well as creating pictures from scratch. These were marked as "unsure" by Pangram, though to cut it some slack, only a small amount of the images were altered.

As with the text, the best way to beat Pangram's detection systems seems to be to include some AI embedded in human-made content. It will most likely still fail the "100% human" test, but the tests I ran revealed that Pangram is less certain in these cases, or underestimates the amount of AI there actually is.

Increase the level of AI, and the detection gets more reliable—but if you're only using AI for a small part of whatever it is you're making, it's less worthwhile using AI tools anyway. As far as these tests go, Pangram's claims about accuracy check out, making it a useful tool if you need to ensure something is AI-free.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.

This is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own. With Alt Video, you do things slightly differently just because of the focus on a different format. So, say you have a Letterboxd account. After exporting some data from your account, you can bring that into Alt Video, and this fake video store will then get filled up with shelves of DVD cases of all the films you've watched.

According to recent reports, alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store. What's more interesting here is that there's a cinema room in the store that lets you watch films on your Plex server, and it's possible to invite your Steam friends to watch along with you. There's even a few other rooms, like a '90s bedroom or family room for more of a CRT kinda vibe. It's cute! If you like you can even manually add any DVDs or Blu-rays you own to appear on all the shelves too.

It has been revealed that there's a lot of other nice touches too. In the case of your Letterboxd data, your ratings even show up on the back of the boxes. It's not just relegated to films either, you can put in demonstrates or even your games. The whole thing can be played in VR if you really want that immersive feel. There's a store clerk who can give you some recommendations if you're not sure what to watch. And there's even a day and night system, weather, and seasonal shopfront facelifts.

Industry observers note that alt Video is presently slated for release next week on November 24th, and it'll be doing so in early access. Worth noting that for now the focus is on the browsing, but features involving serving customers and running the store are on the way. You can wishlist it on Steam right here.
