📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I thought every male actor between the ages of 20 and 60 had auditioned to be the fresh Bond, but apparently at least one beloved star didn't get a chance to try on the tux: Charlie Cox. According to the Marvel star, he wanted to audition for Bond 26, but Amazon’s response was pretty mean-spirited. It also makes little sense, considering who we now know landed the job.

Sources indicate that there's already been a ton of discussion about casting the next Bond movie, which Denis Villeneuve is set to direct. Cox offered a pretty entertaining perspective on the Bond search. During an appearance on Virgin Radio UK's The Chris Evans Breakfast Show, he talked about Pattinson landing the iconic role, then revealed he'd asked for his own shot. His account of the response honestly made me wince a little:.

Industry observers note that can I say something? I asked to audition for that. Do you know what they told me? ‘Too old.’ But Rob is the same age as me! He does look good for it, I have to be fair. Next [month] I am going to be 44… how is 44 too old?

Recent findings suggest that not to call the guy out, but a small correction to Cox's math: he's at the moment 43 and will turn 44 in December, while Pattinson is 40. They're not quite the same age, as host Chris Evans pointed out during the conversation. Three years does seem like a pretty small age gap when you're talking about two established actors being considered for a role. Especially since it's a part neither of them would have probably landed in their twenties.

Bond's age is a fair consideration for producers, especially when the movies can take years to make, and an actor might play 007 for more than a decade. There's plenty of precedent for casting someone in their 40s. Daniel Craig was 38 when Casino Royale arrived in 2006 and 53 when No Time to Die ended his run in 2021. Roger Moore was 45 when he debuted in 1973's Live and Let Die. Looking at those numbers, I don't think Cox was asking for anything outrageous. He's 43, just three years older than Pattinson, and wasn't even given the chance to audition.

In fairness, I can understand a casting team having a particular vision for the part. I can even understand an age cutoff, if I don't particularly agree with it. Still, there's something especially deflating about being ruled out before anyone sees what you might bring to the character.

Recent findings suggest that the whole thing is even funnier because Cox and Pattinson go way back. They were part of a circle of young actors that also included Jamie Dornan, Andrew Garfield and Eddie Redmayne. Cox spoke warmly about his friend's career during the radio interview, complimenting the filmmakers Pattinson worked with before they became major names. He also admitted he had expected Jack Lowden or Callum Turner to get the Bond job, so the eventual casting surprised him, too.

Cox has plenty going on regardless. He's preparing to appear in The King's Ransom at London's Donmar Warehouse, and he'll return as Matt Murdock for the third and final season of Daredevil: Born Again. He's certainly proven he can carry an action-heavy franchise.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I'm happy for Pattinson, and Cox clearly is, too. I just wish someone had let the guy read a few lines before deciding he was past his Bond expiration date.

It has been revealed that ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

A VPN is far from necessary for many people, but some like to see what's going on in other countries, or find the security tools offer some peace of mind.

  • According to recent reports, there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped.
  • P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

According to recent reports, there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he remarked in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day.".

Wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus plans to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

"Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries.".

As for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying.".

Recent findings suggest that we don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in my first 30 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I think I saw it rain once. And that was during a particularly gloomy main story mission where it felt like it was intentionally flipped on and not a serendipitous moment created by the game's weather system.

According to recent reports, I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.

Apparently, the questioning was justified: The weather system was broken and should now be fixed in a new patch that went out today.

"Fixed an problem that resulted in weather not changing for extended periods," the patch notes say, confirming that, while some players witnessed changes in weather, it was not properly happening at the rate it was intended.

In a recent development, you don't partner with The Weather Channel to post exclusive pre-release screenshots of your game if the forecast is mostly sunny and not actually representative of Florida, the state with the most unpredictable weather in the US. GTA 6 has realistically detailed radio towers that left a TikTok guy who's worked on them in real life gobsmacked. It would've been bizarre if Rockstar neglected to put that kind of effort into a system normies like me would notice within a few hours.

The sun's reign is over and all the other meteorological conditions can take the spotlight. As someone who takes their time doing all the silly little daily routines in Jason and Lucia's life and abiding by traffic laws for the vibes, I'm excited to see how much the weather affects the mood. I'll just have to remember to be a little more discerning when chasing down one of GTA 6's cars to make sure I don't absolutely ruin the interior from a surprise storm.

One Regret Prince William Allegedly Has Amid His Estrangement From Prince Harry And Meghan Markle.

Latest Update: Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1364 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change.
  • Download your playlist as a .txt file.
  • In a recent development, install Python on your system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

In a recent development, install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

It has been revealed that have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

Like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of new-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection.".

On Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. Customers can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

It has been revealed that if you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Pick your speaker on your wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

Plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

In a recent development, tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:.

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

Exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

Set your levels with the mixer’s faders.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:.

In a recent development, mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

My cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

It's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:.

In a recent development, your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

According to recent reports, most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. Here's when to turn down the settings:.

When you're in your car: CarPlay and Bluetooth cut audio down to CD quality or less before it reaches your speaker, and with road noises, it usually doesn't matter anyway, so turn the streaming down to "High" instead of "Max." Or download your playlist before you leave, if you must have "as good as possible" audio.

You have a data cap and are off wifi. Top quality audio requires huge file transfer, so set your mobile data to High or Low and save Max for wifi.

Your connection is spotty: To avoid buffering, a lower setting keeps the music playing.

According to recent reports, this isn't a universal hack, but some Android phones have microSD card slots, which can save you a lot of hassle if you're downloading a lot of audio files—an album at high quality might top 1GB, so having an external source will save you a ton of hassle. If your phone has a microSD card slot, go to Tidal's settings, find "download destination" and choose the memory card.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nobody should be surprised how much of the discourse around GTA 6 has pivoted on Jason being some sort of simp for Lucia.
  • Michael 'Cromwelp' Douse, the director of publishing at Larian, provides some expanded thoughts on his time in Leonida thus far on Twitter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nobody should be surprised how much of the discourse around GTA 6 has pivoted on Jason being some sort of simp for Lucia. Disappointed nonetheless, sure, but not surprised. Regardless, a senior member of Baldur's Gate 3 tech giant Larian Studios commends Rockstar for injecting more humanity than ever into the cast here.

Michael 'Cromwelp' Douse, the director of publishing at Larian, provides some expanded thoughts on his time in Leonida thus far on Twitter. "I really like GTA 6's near-organic morality system," he starts. "The quality of assets, writing and storytelling are such that it makes sense to be able to do a lot for the characters (substantial and small) that resonate, while allowing for you to be a shit-head with folks outside of the network, or the neighborhood.".

According to recent reports, he points towards the way you fulfill errands and do small favors to earn people's trust, all the while the game is teaching us about who these characters really are. "Like tipping bar owner in her 60s as she's sweetly smiling, dancing to the veteran house band at a dive bar get-together," he writes. "Picking up an alcoholics' favorite rum as a human gesture of good will.".

According to recent reports, I realllllly like GTA6s near-organic morality system. The quality of assets, writing and storytelling are such that it makes sense to be able to do a lot for the characters (big and small) that resonate, while allowing for you to be a shit-head with folks outside of the network, or the neighborhood. Of course, a lot of that is authored by the developers but the breadth & quality of assets, animations and characters make a lot of it organic, too. Like tipping bar owner in her 60s as she's sweetly smiling, dancing to the veteran house band at a dive bar get-together. Picking up an alcoholics' favorite rum as a human gesture of good will. Acknowledging vices, and doing little 'quests' for the people in your life bring a newly introduced context to the acts of violence that make the game so cathartic. And those are fun. Everything in this game has been scaled up, and so too have the organic relationships between the caricatures of life. This game isn't trying to make you a simp, it is just daring you to (thanks in part to it's technical prowess) to see the wold's characters as human beings. In its success of this it is remarkable. It tries to give everyone and everything a soul so that whatever you do has greater meaning and that added depth is pretty unique, so I understand why the discourse is split. The line between character and caricature in this one is very blurry, and I think that's neat.November 22, 2026.

There are many such examples, but some of the loudest voices on the collective internet have zeroed in on these aspects and used them to accuse the game of being "woke" or turning players into simps because Jason actively cares about Lucia's well-being. The complaints are shallow and asinine, but Douse addresses them directly.

Recent findings suggest that "Everything in this game has been scaled up, and so too have the organic relationships between the caricatures of life," he says. "This game isn't trying to make you a simp, it is just daring you (thanks in part to its technical prowess) to see the world's characters as human beings.".

He calls GTA 6 "remarkable" in how well it manages to do all of this. I do applaud Rockstar for rejecting power fantasy in favor of grounding the protagonists in a world where the mundane is embraced rather than rejected. Being a decent person isn't simp behaviour, and I'd be wary of anyone trying to say otherwise.

  • In a recent development, the Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st.
  • Sources indicate that original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have quickly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An upgrade for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently unveiled the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.

In a recent development, the Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st. In the interim, a Reddit user with the handle ShweetsStuff unearthed metadata pointing to AI tune generator Suno attached to some of the update's music files. Cue understandable questioning of why the DLC's Steam page hadn't had a disclosure of this genAI use slapped across it.

Sources indicate that original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have quickly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action. "Woke up to a shit show," he posted on the former Twitterverse on the 21st. Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.".

Given the new build yanking the music went live later that day, McMillen's voice maybe only added to the chorus of complaints Nicalis were already aware of and facing. Either way, the songs are gone and Nicalis don't look to have mentioned anything as of writing about whether they'll be replaced at some point down the line.

This isn't the first time a developer has considered using AI to generate songs designed to satirise or parody. In the case of Future? No Thanks! dev Paolo 'Molleindustria' Pedercini, the aim was partly to poke fun at disclosures, with people in the game's future society listening to AI-generated tunes that're corporately mandated to mention AI in the lyrics. Pedercini ended up deciding not to use AI-generated music in the final release.

According to recent reports, on the face of it, while the effectiveness of using AI-generated songs to parody AI-generated songs is questionable, the argument for it seems stronger in a more focused satire like Future? No Thanks! than in the case of The Binding of Isaac having a GTA 6-related giggle. I've not listened to the Repentance+ enhancement's AI tunes, but there's nothing obvious to indicate that their satirical job wouldn't have been done as well or better by Nicalis commissioning or otherwise employing someone to pen some entirely human-made ditties, that spoofed the nature of Large Stealy Wheely.

Perhaps the publishers will now go and do just that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.

As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a fresh record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

Recent findings suggest that for context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

Industry observers note that "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," stated Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you.".

Previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

Sources indicate that every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent organization Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't stated anything concrete about that just yet.

It has been revealed that "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I recently switched music streamers from Apple Music to Tidal. I like Tidal's strict anti-AI features, the fact that it pays higher royalties to artists than other major streamers, and its focus on high quality audio. I wrote a post featuring eight hacks for Tidal owners, but I wanted to highlight one in particular: How to transfer playlists without paying anything.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Recent findings suggest that install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Industry observers note that sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Sources indicate that have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap.
  • In a recent development, the hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website.
  • "Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected users was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.

In a recent development, the hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website. It's designed to address one issue, this being that "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background".

"Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix. "This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is important to many users might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to promptly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the hotfix driver will be taken down.

It has been revealed that "To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more quickly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out.".

Unfortunately, it seems that based on some testing by people on r/Nvidia, the hotfix makes the situation with excessive SSD writing less bad than it is with 621.24, but doesn't eliminate the problem entirely. According to one of these users, 621.35 stops the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reduces the amount that's being written when the issue's at its peak, but doesn't prevent some excessive writing creeping in if hardware is left running for extended periods or left idling overnight.

According to recent reports, given that, rolling back to 621.01 still appears to be the most effective way of keeping the writes at an acceptable level while waiting for Nvidia to release a new driver than can permanently do away with the problem. One would hope it won't take too long, especially given the 621.24 driver still doesn't look to have been pulled offline so no one else grabs it prior to a fix arriving.

If you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's only writing a matter of MB or chunks of GB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the first non-binary character in the series' history, according to actor Jesse James Rose, who plays the role of a museum curator in the game.

"I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago.".

It has been revealed that "I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

"GTA was one of the most inclusive & caring sets I've ever been on," they added.

A post shared by Jesse James Rose ✨ (@jamesissmiling).

The role was shot entirely through motion capture, which meant wearing "a unitard made of dots every day". Rose also notes steps were taken to protect the character in-game: "To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character.".

Recent findings suggest that A whole day of the shoot was spent scanning Rose's face, including hours of pulling different expressions. At one point Rose couldn't move a particular muscle, and worried the scan had been ruined, but the director was thrilled.

Industry observers note that "That right there is exactly why we'll never use AI," he mentioned, according to Rose. "A computer could never come up with the face you just made.".

"Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labour to preserve the integrity of the game," Rose added.

Rose did raise some concerns about pay, though.

"Despite being paid well for my time on set, I'll never see a residual check for my work," Rose wrote, explaining that this is part of SAG’s contract with game developers. As a union leader at one of SAG's sister unions, Rose mentioned there's still "a long way to go to ensure arts workers are fairly compensated for our labour".

Recent findings suggest that rose also says many other trans people worked on GTA 6, both in front of the camera and behind it. "SO many trans people besides me are featured in GTA VI as other roles, designers, writers, etc... take a note, theatre and TV! We are employable & profitable!!!".

Recent findings suggest that finally, Rose voiced support for Rockstar's UK staff. "UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are presently voting on whether to unionise, and I sincerely hope their efforts are successful," Rose wrote. "Every arts worker should have a stable job with benefits and fair working conditions protected by a union.".

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It launched on Thursday, although some have been getting in on the action earlier, as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Newly introduced Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Grand Theft Auto 6 is enjoying what may very well be the single greatest media launch in history, securing over $3.7 billion in launch sales. But as Rockstar enjoys its acclaim, other developers—like Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski—are professing some anxiety about releasing their own games in a post-GTA 6 world.

According to recent reports, "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle," Sarzynski said on Bluesky over the weekend, joking that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled.".

That news came as a surprise to Cyberpunk 2 lead writer Anna Megill, who replied with a baffled "But wait—".

Sarzynski was, of course, just goofing. But I'm sympathetic to any game dev who might be feeling an amount of apprehension about being measured against GTA 6's success, particularly when there's a genre overlap.

Industry observers note that in Cyberpunk 2's case, however, CD Projekt is very much in its own lane: Cyberpunk is a different thematic setting, with entirely different systems and design goals. I'd hope that any reasonable person would think comparing the two is like comparing apples and oranges—particularly when the oranges reportedly had a production budget upwards of $1 billion.

In a follow-up post, Sarzynski acknowledged that each project is doing its own thing, while noting that GTA 6's example will benefit other game developers by serving as a source of creative inspiration.

"Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he mentioned. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is: It expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed.".

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (695 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Eight Important Router Settings You Should Check (or Change)

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet.
  • Your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network.
  • Some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet. This also makes it a highly valuable target for attackers and can leave your data vulnerable—especially if you simply plug your router in with its default settings unchanged. Whether your router is brand newly introduced or it's been a while since you audited your existing setup, these are the key settings to check and change right now.

Your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network. WPA3 Personal is the newest standard and the most secure, so if it's available on your router, enable it. It's compatible with devices that support Wi-Fi 6. Some older devices may not work with WPA3, in which case the WPA2/WPA3 Transitional mixed mode is a good alternative. At minimum, set your router to WPA2 Personal (AES).

Some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard. (This is not the same as your network name or wifi password, which you set up later.) Default router passwords are searchable online, which leaves your router's admin settings open to anyone. Once you get into your dashboard for the first time, change the default credentials and enable two-factor authentication for your admin account if available.

While some newer routers do have unique, device-specific defaults, it's a good idea to check this setting and ensure it's secure. If you're prompted to create custom admin credentials during the setup process, do it.

It has been revealed that your network name, or SSID, is how your network appears when you search for available wifi. By default, this may be the name of the router brand or a short string of characters, but you should choose something unique to your network. Make sure there's no identifying personal information, such as your name or house number. While you may be tempted to hide your network and obscure your SSID, this may actually make your information less secure, so keep this setting disabled. You can, however, add "_nomap" to the end of your network name, which prevents your router's physical coordinates from being mapped by location databases.

The password to access your network should also be unique and secure and should not include obvious personal information. One option to keep it memorable and easy to type is to create a passphrase using five to seven unrelated words that, combined, have at least 16 characters.

Recent findings suggest that two additional settings that leave your network vulnerable are Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) and Universal Plug and Play (UPnP). The former lets users connect to your network with a PIN, which can be vulnerable to brute-force attacks. The latter allows smart devices to easily connect to your network—but this also allows malware to spread more readily. You may need to have UPnP on in order to connect devices initially but should disable it afterward.

Any easy win for your network security is segmenting traffic to different networks, so if one is compromised, the data on the others remain unaffected. Many wifi routers have a "guest mode," which creates a separate SSID and password that you can share with visitors instead of giving them your primary network credentials. You can also set up a separate network for all of your smart home and IoT devices so exploitable vulnerabilities in these devices don't put your computers, phones, and other connected devices at risk too.

Routers run a type of software—called firmware—just like any other device. Firmware controls the router's core functions and is not immune to vulnerabilities, which can be exploited by bad actors. And, just like other types of software, manufacturers occasionally push updates to patch these flaws. Check your router's dashboard to see if automatic updates are toggled on. Some devices require an opt-in for auto updates during setup, so you should enable them if they are off. Some routers may even require manual updates—in this case, set a monthly or quarterly (at minimum) calendar reminder to check for patches.

Tech Report: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that 1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild.
  • In a recent development, in much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it.
  • In a recent development, in the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that 1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In a recent development, in much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise newly introduced players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.

In a recent development, in the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies. "They've gone into these levels in a sensible way to fix some practical problems with them, like some issues where you might be able to climb up to a place that you shouldn't have been able to climb up before," he commented.

The Thief remaster team have taken more liberties, seemingly, with some of the Thief Gold maps. "Because some of the levels that were introduced in Thief Gold - they felt quite blocky and quite rushed, maybe, as you go through them," Grayshon explained. "But our team again, they've been able to go through and completely renovate some of these levels. The Opera House now feels in some parts like an actual Opera House, instead of a couple of blocky rooms. So I think players will really look at these and think, oh yeah, these kinds of details make sense, without it being too disruptive or too immersion breaking…".

"One particular - maybe people will consider infamous - level of the Gold package would be the Thieves Guild," Grayshon added. "The Thieves Guild is, if I were to sum it up kind of briefly, it is maybe two hours of walking through what feels like sewers, the same environment over and over again. There was no real visual distinction as to where you are in the level.

"So, we acknowledged pretty promptly that we need to go in and look at the Thieves Guild and fix it up, and what we've been able to do is texture it a lot more effectively. Give areas distinct looks, without compromising any of the gameplay again, like I mentioned. So we've put a bit more signposting around as well. Nothing that's going to be intrusive or immersion breaking again. Just kind of pointing the player in the right direction, as well as some other little things that I'm not going to spoil too much, but I think players will maybe appreciate the effort that we've done for this one.".

According to recent reports, in general, Nightdive's broad aim has been "bringing those Gold levels up to the quality of the original and then taking all of those levels and then bumping them up to the next level - almost Thief 2 levels of quality in its environment design, especially in some of the mansions, and some of the later levels," Grayshon mentioned. "That's the level we were aiming for.".

I have Several Thoughts about Grayshon's thoughts above (yes, people who dislike huffy armchair theory, this is your cue to skip to the comments). One is that I continue to dislike "immersion" as an ideal, though I recognise that many devs just use it as easy shorthand for a bunch of ways of doing art, sound and interface design. I think it often translates to uninvestigated enthusiasm for photorealistic fidelity and experiences that feel "smooth" and "engaging" enough to induce a kind of chemical trance. Many of the games I consider most valuable are cranky and unwilling and jarring, requiring you to think critically about the simulation rather than 'losing yourself' inside it. As regards the original Thief specifically, I enjoy how its nigh-magical stealth induces feelings of wavering dissociation, and keeps me guessing about the solidity of my own body.

Secondly, there's the age-old argument that if you're going to preserve a game faithfully, you should preserve what it did badly. The Thieves Guild is a legend among players, much as Blighttown is among Dark Souls players and the Library is among fans of Halo: Combat Evolved. You learn much about the methodology of Thief at large from the guild's stifling contours, and it's thrilling to witness a bunch of very smart designers take a swing at a concept and not quite connect. I'll try to hold onto that rousing sentiment, when I'm playing the remaster and struggling to remember where they hid that damn vase.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I've sat through Ryan Murphy's takes on Jeffrey Dahmer and Lizzie Borden, so I'm no stranger to true-crime dramas that seem determined to make audiences uncomfortable.
  • It has been revealed that the trailer begins on Dec.
  • The preview then moves into the investigation and the attention that followed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I've sat through Ryan Murphy's takes on Jeffrey Dahmer and Lizzie Borden, so I'm no stranger to true-crime dramas that seem determined to make audiences uncomfortable. But after watching the trailer for Netflix's upcoming The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey, which premieres as part of the 2026 TV schedule, I felt more uneasy than I ever did watching either of those productions. The trailer itself is surprisingly restrained, and Melissa McCarthy looks terrific as Patsy Ramsey, alongside Clive Owen as her husband, John. Nothing in the footage is particularly shocking, at least by the standards we've come to expect from the genre. Yet I finished watching it with a sinking feeling I haven't quite been able to shake.

It has been revealed that the trailer begins on Dec. 26, 1996, with McCarthy's Patsy making the frantic 911 call reporting that her daughter is missing. Police arrive at the Boulder, Colorado, house, and the family highlights them a ransom note. We know how the search ends: JonBenét is found dead in the basement. Watching actors retrace those hours, even briefly, made me uncomfortable. The sequence feels eerily familiar because so many of us have heard the details repeated for decades.

The preview then moves into the investigation and the attention that followed. Officers question what happened inside the home, reporters crowd the family, and suspicion increasingly falls on the parents. McCarthy's Patsy breaks down, insisting, "I didn't kill my baby." There's also a chilling moment when the district attorney, played by Shea Whigham, acknowledges that even the facts investigators can establish may never satisfy a public desperate for an explanation. It's a trailer built around grief and accusation, with no resolution waiting at the end.

It has been revealed that I think a lot of that comes down to remembering that JonBenét Ramsey was just 6 years old when she was murdered in 1996. Nearly 30 years later, her killing remains unsolved; nobody has been convicted, and her mother died in 2006 without ever seeing someone brought to justice for her daughter's death. In the decades since, JonBenét's murder has become the subject of countless documentaries, television specials, and endless speculation. Netflix itself released another docuseries about the case in 2024.

I understand that this new production may be trying to examine the media circus surrounding her death, and perhaps it will handle that responsibly. But watching the trailer, I couldn't stop thinking about how much entertainment we've already made out of this little girl's murder. Hasn't JonBenét Ramsey's death made enough money for other people?

According to recent reports, the people making this series seem aware of that problem. McCarthy has spoken about how the public fascination with the mystery overshadowed the fact that parents lost their child, and Netflix notes the drama examines the consequences of the media frenzy. I appreciate that intention. Richard LaGravenese, the showrunner, is telling a story that cannot provide the ending audiences have spent years demanding. Boulder police still describe JonBenét's murder as an active investigation.

Maybe the full series will find a thoughtful way to reckon with all of that. I'm certainly not questioning McCarthy's performance based on the footage we've seen. I just keep thinking about the difference between watching a fictional horror story and revisiting a real child's death for entertainment. The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey premieres on Netflix Dec. 10 for everyone with a Netflix subscription. I'm not sure yet whether I'll be able to watch it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

While critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".

The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take issue with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

Sources indicate that "Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and fresh features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality.".

Sources indicate that "Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience.

According to recent reports, "The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****.".

Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas.

In a recent development, "A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," mentioned one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close.".

GTA 6 launched on Thursday for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Earlier today, actor Jesse James Rose revealed the game features the series' first non-binary character.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A BioWare veteran who most recently worked on Mass Effect 5 doesn't have much hope EA will sell the IP. In fact, they reckon it'll be a "miracle" if we get another RPG, book, or comic.

News of BioWare's closure and the cancellation of Mass Effect 5 (Universe, as it was called) came following the recent EA buyout – news that hasn't exactly gone over well with fans eagerly awaiting the studio's now-dead RPG.

In fact, it spurred an entire movement and the Save Mass Effect petition, which garnered thousands of signatures. Heck, fans even gathered outside of EA offices to protest the death of what might have been the biggest Mass Effect to date – but in terms of any concrete word on a revival of sorts… Well, there's been nothing. And, sadly, it's likely to stay that way, as former Mass Effect Universe developer and Annihilation author Cat Valente admits.

According to recent reports, she implies as much over on Reddit, telling a fan that she's not sure another publisher or company will swoop in and somehow buy BioWare in hopes of saving the Mass Effect team, or that the franchise will see a comeback: "I want to be wrong, I truly do. But because I am a gamer, despite what the hordes of X would say, I've been burned by EA before and I don't really believe in my heart they'll let it go.".

Recent findings suggest that valente continues, explaining that any offshoot of the series would be nothing short of "a miracle" – should it ever happen in the first place – and will likely have to do with the Mass Effect TV show. "If they allow books or comics or RPGs or something of the sort, that will be a miracle, but probably be connected to the show (if that happens, it's been in development hell forever) than anything I ever worked on or even the trilogy," she says.

None of this means Valente doesn't want more Mass Effect. "I want to believe! I cried seeing that billboard in Times Square. I think the last 10 years have made me into a cynic when it comes to enshittification, and because I poured years of my finite mortal life into this, it hurts too much to hope, so I prepare myself for disappointment," she states. Not to mention that, uh, if anything did come to fruition, it might not be… ideal.

Sources indicate that it would never be from the BioWare fans grew to love over three decades. "Especially since, if it did get a new home, it almost certainly wouldn't include much or anything of what I (or our team) did," as Valente describes. "A new owner would want to put their own spin on it and start from scratch – maybe people would be hired back, maybe not, but it's hard to see a way that what I worked on would be what a totally different studio felt beholden to.".

She doesn't want the community to give up hope, though: "Don't stop fighting, don't stop believing, hold the line, prove me wrong." Unfortunately, however, Valente isn't the only one who feels… uncertain. Another ex-dev stated "EA never actually sells anything" and we shouldn't expect a rekindling of Universe as "they just shut things down and sit on their licenses." You know, like American McGee's Alice.

Much like Valente and other past devs, I wouldn't hold my breath – but I also agree that fans shouldn't abandon all hope, as every desired outcome has to start somewhere. It's evident that Mass Effect isn't going down without stirring a storm, at least.

Mass Effect Universe would "clean up" Mass Effect 3's endings "in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off," writer notes.

After spending years with her head in various fantastical realms' clouds, Anna studied English Literature and then Medieval History at the University of Edinburgh, going on to specialize in narrative design and video game journalism as a writer. She has written for various publications since her postgraduate studies, including Dexerto, Fanbyte, GameSpot, IGN, PCGamesN, and more. When she's not frantically trying to form words into coherent sentences, she's probably daydreaming about becoming a fairy druid and befriending every animal or she's spending a thousand (more) hours traversing the Underdark in Baldur's Gate 3. If you spot her away from her PC, you'll always find Anna with a fantasy book, a handheld video game console of some sort, and a Tamagotchi or two on hand.

  • According to recent reports, apple is currently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure.
  • With the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

According to recent reports, apple is currently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other fresh features. But for customers of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

With the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first fresh iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This update just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

It has been revealed that now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software enhancement can introduce latest hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

Industry observers note that what's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

Sources indicate that apple made a significant deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That mentioned, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

Sources indicate that iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some people may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the newly introduced option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.

Winterkeep Interactive is led by Mattias Wiking, Petter Nallo, Karl Emdin, Frida Eriksson and Ola Enberg, and comprised of Paradox Interactive veterans whose previous credits include titles such as Stellaris, Crusader Kings II, Europa Universalis IV, Victoria 3, and other games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A BBC report says Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again.

It has been revealed that kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served. He was given a five-year "Serious Crime Prevention Order" restricting his allowable online activity, including bans on using Telegram and Discord.

Recent findings suggest that "Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement," Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police stated following Kurtaj's sentencing and release. "We hope this case serves as a lesson that these types of acts will not be tolerated.

"Although cyber crime is borderless, we will seek to utilise the co-operation of partner agencies and international law enforcement to ensure that offenders are brought to justice no matter where they offend from."Kurtaj carried out hacks against multiple companies when he was 16 and 17 years old, including Microsoft, Samsung, Nvidia and UK telecom firm BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals.

But it was his hack of Rockstar and leak of GTA 6 materials more than a year before it was formally revealed, that earned him notoriety, not least because of how it was carried out: While under police protection in a Travelodge hotel room, using an Amazon Fire Stick and a mobile phone.

A psychiatric assessment determined that Kurtaj had "acute autism," and that he "continued to express the intent to return to cybercrime as soon as possible" while he was in custody. That led to his hospital sentence, but earlier this year he was found fit to stand trial and subsequently pleaded guilty to all charges.

Recent findings suggest that that struck me as odd—why plead guilty to crimes carried out at a time when your mental state was such that a court decided you required multiple years of institutionalization?—but this may be the answer: Kurtaj, now 21, is a free man. The judge on the case told Kurtaj he is "a very talented young man," but also warned him: "Don't let this happen again.".

Some Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PS5 say the game keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1, and in some cases, it's stopping them from progressing through the story.

According to recent reports, "The game runs perfectly fine for a while. I can complete missions and chapters without any issues, but then it suddenly crashes after around 40 minutes and sends me back to the PS5 home screen", wrote one Reddit user. They added that other games, including GTA 5 and For Honor, run without crashing.

Another player told Dexerto that GTA 6 worked fine until Pipework, an early mission that introduces Mandy, but now crashes "every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it", which means they can’t progress.

Some PS5 Pro owners say the game crashes during the opening prologue, either at the same point every time or a few seconds in, and they haven't been able to play since launch.

Others say they've tried the usual fixes, such as clearing their console's cache, rebuilding the database, factory resetting their PS5, and even downloading the game three times, but nothing has worked thus far.

It's not just PS5 players that are struggling, either; some Xbox Series X players have reported crashes too, with one saying the game sometimes crashes after just 15 minutes.

Rockstar hasn't yet acknowledged the crashes or stated whether a patch is on the way, and its own support is sending players with console errors to PlayStation or Xbox directly for help.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, there's no firm fix just yet. PlayStation's support page describes CE-108255-1 simply as "an error occurred with the game/application”, and its only advice is to "try updating your game". It's a solid choice for gaming, especially at this price point.

Alienware makes great gaming laptops, and the Aurora is a great option for anyone who wants to get all the essentials without spending too much. At its current $1,099 price (originally $1,999), the Alienware Aurora 16 becomes a mid-tier gaming laptop at a "budget" price. We reviewed the higher-tier Aurora 16X and were impressed with it. The Aurora 16 has a slightly slower processor, a dimmer display with half the refresh rate, a smaller battery, and a weaker graphics card, but given its price, it's great for a gamer looking for a solid gaming laptop in the $1,000 range.

In a recent development, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Amazon has a much larger inventory of tech products on sale, but the ones they both sell are mostly priced the same. While Amazon may have more deals, Walmart usually has a couple of surprise flagship tech products on sale that Amazon will later price match. So taking all of that into consideration, the best one will be whichever has whatever you're looking to buy at the lower price.

As a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's notable questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.

In this first-person co-op platformer - created in Unreal Engine, with both online multiplayer and splitscreen support - you and a mate play Luna and Foam, two rock-hopping magic children with nothing better to do than lob hermetically sealed felines through tears in reality itself. Egad! Apparently the cats are fine with this. You'll have to work together to traverse astral watercolour landscapes, hurling and catching the kitty while trying not to tumble into the abyss.

You can also catch each other's arms and haul each other onto safe ground, which puts this in approximately the same bracket as the well-liked Peak. Other Neat Tricks include bouncing the starry-eyed moggies from soap bubbles, swinging from strands of green snot (?), and springboarding from tornadoes.

Recent findings suggest that the cats remain blissfully unconscious throughout, smiling in their slumber right up to the point when you crack their crystal prisons. If you're familiar with cats, the penalty for breaking their domes may seem rather mild. I was hoping for something along the lines of Peter Puppy having a rage-out in Earthworm Jim.

Industry observers note that would it surprise you to learn that one or more of the people working on Whisk is a former developer of Sky: Children of Light, the open world swoop 'em up from thatgamecompany? I imagine you might not consider that startling – the two games both look a little like the result of somebody inhaling burnt banana skins. But you might be giddier to hear that one or more of the Whisk devs is also a veteran of Riot's Counter-Strike descendant Valorant. I'm pretty sure Valorant doesn't have any cat-throwing, but I'm prepared to be proven wrong.

Industry observers note that it's coming to Steam early access early in 2027, and there's a demo on Steam right now with eight levels and 10 cats to "rescue". People are already bragging in the forums about their leaderboard placements – monsters!

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence.
  • In a recent development, kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.

Industry observers note that the BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence. On licence means his release is subject to a number of conditions. According to the UK Government website, the exact nature of these conditions varies from person to person and case to case, as they've got be "considered necessary and proportionate". However, things like needing not to commit any more crimes, not travel abroad, and live under the supervision of community offender manager are cited as part of a set of "standard licence conditions" outlined by the government site.

In a recent development, kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online. It includes bans from using both Telegram and Discord.

According to the BBC, the judge told Kurtaj Yyou are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again." City of London Police remarked the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

It has been revealed that kurtaj pleaded guilty on November 16th at Woolwich Crown Court to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack, as well as a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Now aged 21, he was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely, due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial.

In a recent development, 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by the 2022 hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the tech giant contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

It has been revealed that earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by 'Cyberleek' posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent tech giant Take-Two promptly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

In a recent development, cyberleek has since claimed to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 onto the net, while withholding a main executable file they threatened to release subsequently. Online sources claim the executable has now also been leaked, though this has not been independently verified.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phasmophobia's next update, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-new piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.

In a recent development, the headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School. As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

Industry observers note that the Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

Recent findings suggest that you'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and latest buttons let you quickly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," noted Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive.".

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free revision and will be available on all platforms.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Patch. The studio ended up apologising to players for problems with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".
