📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If the first season of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County was any indication, there is no shortage of drama where those women, Mormon or not, are concerned. I’m thrilled to learn that the Hulu series that debuted on the 2026 TV schedule has been renewed for 20 episodes, which likely means we’re guaranteed even more than just Season 2. Although there is one big change that I want to see as the series moves forward.

It has been revealed that yes, the OC spinoff has its own cast of women connected to the Mormon religion, this time living in Southern California instead of Utah. I am sure there are plenty of stories still to be explored with them as individuals, as well as with the tension in their relationships and friendships. However, with Jen Affleck doing double duty on the OG and OC Mormon Wives reality reveals (which are streaming with a Hulu subscription), and McCall DePron being the older sister of Mayci Neeley, we absolutely need to see more of the women who started this franchise making appearances on the new series.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives original series has had a seemingly endless amount of drama and scandals, but things crossed a line into serious domestic and custody disputes in a shortened Season 5 of only five episodes that made it all less fun to watch. While the decision to include women who are not Mormon in the Orange County series is a bit strange, having more appearances from the OG cast would help resolve that matter.

Sources indicate that after the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody complications with her children, and chaos surrounding production of the original series, I will say upfront that we don’t need to see Taylor Frankie Paul head over to the OC with her brand of drama. But after Mayci apologized for crossing the line in defense of her sister McCall, I’d be down to see her and Mikayla Matthews, as well as Layla Taylor, Jessi Ngatikaura, and even Miranda McWhorter show up in sunny Southern California. I feel like not only could any or all of those women bring some fun to the spinoff, but they could also inject some more Mormon energy into the mix.

According to recent reports, because Mormon Wives OC’s first season had to introduce us to a lot of newly introduced women, there wasn’t much time in its eight episodes to let us see much of their home lives, families, and relationships. Since it was also introducing many of those women to each other, some of the tension and confrontations felt more manufactured and forced.

Recent findings suggest that now that they’re going into Season 2 with more familiarity, hopefully interactions will start to feel more organic. On top of that, if you bring more original cast members to Orange County, they could provide unique perspectives on their own Mormon lifestyle in Utah while also creating new conflicts and storylines for fans of both demonstrates to get excited about and debate.

Sources indicate that in other news, fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt is getting her own reality show, so we likely won’t see her back in the Mormon Wives world, at least anytime soon (never say never, right?). But with 20 new episodes guaranteed with the OC spinoff, I know I’ll be seated and waiting for all the drama to come.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.
  • "… We will continue to take community feedback into account as we carefully evaluate the possibility of permanently enabling travel between the North American and European data centers, as well as opening travel between other physical data centers," via the Lodestone.
  • Industry observers note that I play Final Fantasy 14 on the US servers—which is a problem, because I live in the UK.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

"… We will continue to take community feedback into account as we carefully evaluate the possibility of permanently enabling travel between the North American and European data centers, as well as opening travel between other physical data centers," via the Lodestone.

This is a significant deal and I'm very excited.

Industry observers note that I play Final Fantasy 14 on the US servers—which is a problem, because I live in the UK. I do so because, well, some of my closest friends are on those servers, too; but also because there's a slightly livelier roleplay community bustling on the US side of things, and I'm a roleplayer who likes squeezing my warrior of light like he's a stress toy.

As a result, I've often stared longingly at the people who play in the UK due to the crime of my time zone: Unable to play with my UK friends, unable to join a static raiding group that starts at a reasonable hour, and unable to play the game without terrible animation lock on my abilities. Unless I, say, broke ToS and used an addon that brought me on-par with people who have 30 ping, hypothetically. Which I don't do.

Square Enix has thrown open these doors, however, to mainly deal with congestion troubles:.

"As peak play times differ between North America and Europe, another physical data center may be less crowded and serve as a viable option when login queues on your usual data center are long. While players connecting from geographically distant locations may experience increased latency, we encourage you to try playing on a different physical data center before the expansion rolls out.".

However, they know that people like me have expressed their yearning to hop between the good ol' USA and Europe: "However, we have received ongoing feedback from players wishing to travel between the North American and European data centers, and many players in both regions are able to communicate in English even when it is not their first language.".

In a recent development, all in all, this'll be a huge quality of life improvement. There might be some difficulties, though: raiding culture can vary drastically even between logical datacenters like Aether and Crystal, let alone between continents. However, I'd be shocked if the differences between US and EU raiding cultures were insurmountable; JP and US? Might be a bigger deal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way's Ally Yahuff and her family are presently embroiled in some drama due to a recent episode. Ally's parents claimed the show scripted their daughter's pregnancy reveal scene. However, the TLC star is now pushing back. As her storyline continues to unfold on the 2026 TV schedule, Ally is suggesting that the only fake element is her parents' latest public response.

During the episode, which is currently streaming for those with an HBO Max subscription, it is stated that Ally's parents declined to continue filming after she revealed she was pregnant with Jonathan Pearce's baby before marriage. After news got out that her parents felt 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way scripted the moment to look more dramatic than it was, Ally contacted @KikiandKibbitz and said the following:.

It's honestly stressing me out because she's literally just doing damage control at this point and making stuff up lol. I don't even know what to do I'm under NDA and I can't say anything but she's twisting things. They really didn't know I was pregnant. Why the hell would I be so stressed out and have a lonely pregnancy if they knew?

Ally's stress makes sense, considering the circumstances. Those who assumed the scene was faked may also assume that her crying in bed after the scene wasn't genuine, and that makes the whole situation seem very dramatic and silly. Additionally, past cast members have claimed 90 Day is faked, and I can imagine it'd feel really rough to have the internet decide a real-life traumatic event was just scripted television.

Industry observers note that while speaking out, Ally went on to claim that her parents' response was fueled by how the moment looked on TV, and not by them looking to set the record straight. In her view, they're just trying to avoid any more blowback from the public watching at home:.

She's ashamed of public scrutiny and is trying to rewrite the narrative. And I can't say anything publicly or call her out because she's my mom. I'm just really disappointed.

Recent findings suggest that once again, 90 Day Fiancé fans keeping up with the 2026 TV schedule are caught in the game of "he said, she said." Like what happened with the drama surrounding Vittorio Palchetti's house not being his actual home, it feels like there's an explanation for all of this. Yet, because the audience was misled from the start, I can't help but feel skeptical of everything.

Why I Have Mixed Feelings On How 90 Day: Hunt For Love Addressed Razvan’s Exit.

On the one hand, I can imagine that parents who would disown their adult child for an unexpected pregnancy would also feel ashamed about being called out for it later. Conversely, Ally was very clearly showing ahead of their substantial reveal, to the point that I'm not sure it was even necessary for Jonathan to state it.

According to recent reports, I guess there are two sides to every story, and two things can be true at once. Ally could've thought she was effectively hiding her pregnancy from her parents, but she was wrong, and they already knew before it was said. They also still could've declined to film after the reveal, because they were upset about officially learning the news and that it was set to air on TV. Perhaps the truth is somewhere in the middle and we'll get some answers on what exactly went down later on.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way continues on TLC on Sundays at 8:00 p.m. ET. I'm addicted to the drama and can't stop watching, even if I don't know the full story. On that note, I can't wait to see what's next for Jonathan and Ally.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chris Evans indicates Marvel bosses Kevin Feige and Lou D’Esposito pitched him a Nomad movie prior to Avengers: Doomsday.

"They remarked, ‘We’d love to continue making movies with you. Steve would no longer be Captain America; he would be Nomad," Evans told Entertainment Weekly. "They sent me a pitch and it was a great pitch. It really was. But for whatever reason at the time, I was very happy with how things wrapped up. It didn’t feel like it was the thing I was looking to do at the time.".

Steve Rogers took on the persona of Nomad in Captain America #180, having given up the Cap mantle after becoming disillusioned with the United States government. Taking the name Nomad because felt like a "man without a country," Steve still defended the innocent from the evils of the world at large... but as more of a vigilante. Think Hawkeye becoming a mask-wearing, street-level vigilante known the Ronin after the Blip. Steve would become Cap again in Captain America #184, however.

How is Steve Rogers even in Avengers: Doomsday, you might ask? Well, all we really know is that it definitely has to do with Loki. In one of the Avengers: Endgame Encore post-credits scenes, he appears at Steve and Peggy's door and tells them he's there to help.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in US theaters on December 18 and a few days earlier in the UK on December 16. For more on the MCU, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar just issued a latest patch for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, targeting a few issues players have been reporting since the game launched last Thursday (19th November).

In a recent development, the 23rd November patch for the game deploys seven major fixes for the game, including a pretty significant bug that prevented phone calls not triggering at certain points, resulting in a scenario where you could be locked out of progressing the game. The official update is titled 'version 01.002.002', and its weighs in at different sizes on different consoles: it's 603.8 MB on PS5, and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X/S.

Thanks to an revision on the Rockstar website, you can read all of the updates that arrive with the latest pathc below.

Recent findings suggest that there have been a few fairly high-profile cases of the autosave not working as the developer intended, leading to a few cases of streamers losing plenty of real-world time thanks to unpredictable auto-save behaviour. JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress on the PS5, for example.

But there's one glitch here the developer hasn't addressed: vignetting. Plenty of players have taken to online communities to complain about the vignette effect that pops into the game - theoretically to help with motion smoothing and various grapihcal elements as the game runs in 30FPS. THe effect is worsened when you're fatigued, hungry, or have some other status effect, but it is present quite a lot of the time, too. Most of the responses to a tweet about the patch posted by the Rockstar Support account reference the vignetting in GTA 6, and the developer has issued no response at the time of writing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office. He asked his chief of staff whether she believed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would survive the impeachment attempt that would soon be rolled out by a member of his own party.

It has been revealed that hegseth was in a precarious position. He had been among the most aggressive champions of the war with Iran, widely seen as the policy most responsible for the shellacking Republicans had taken the night before. Wiles remained officially supportive of Hegseth throughout her time in the White House, but she had harbored concerns about the secretary from the start. She did not believe he was forthright about his skeletons during a rocky confirmation process, and she considered the subsequent Signalgate scandal an amateurish disaster.

Industry observers note that in the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle. She offered her resignation, but Trump declined. On Thursday night, in a contentious meeting in the Oval Office, she offered to resign again. Trump revealed the next day that Wiles would leave the White House for his outside political operation.

In a recent development, hegseth’s fate was still uncertain. A deeply unpopular figure among the American public, presiding over an even more unpopular war, he faced an impeachment push led by Representative Thomas Massie. “He is just failing,” noted Republican senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina—who voted to confirm Hegseth at the start of Trump’s term—in an interview with Vanity Fair. “In the same way that Kristi Noem failed at Homeland Security, he simply doesn’t have the instincts or the prior experience as an executive that is necessary for this particular role.”.

The secretary of defense has now embarked on a campaign to save his job, and Stephen Miller’s elevation to replace Wiles as Trump’s chief of staff has helped to ensure a reprieve. Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.” And there are other reasons to keep him in place, the official remarked: Confirming a replacement will not be easy, particularly when Democrats take control of Congress, and ousting Hegseth would signal an admission that at this point, Trump’s war is a failure.

It was the president’s taste for staffers out of central casting that helped put Hegseth—a weekend morning television host with no experience in government, but with the square jaw of an Army Wives extra—in charge of the Department of Defense. He has relied on his talents before the cameras, and a team of advisers attuned to the production of his persona, to both keep his job and sell Trump on aggressive military action from the Pacific to the Persian Gulf. His survival has depended in part on his ability to project strength—not to the public, or to the rank-and-file, but to the president.

“In just under two years, Secretary Hegseth has worked side-by-side with President Trump to restore American power on the world stage, build the strongest military in generations, and instill a warrior ethos at the Pentagon,” White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales remarked in a statement. “President Trump and Secretary Hegseth have taken bold, necessary action to deny the Iranian regime the ability to develop a nuclear weapon, bring narco-terrorist Nicolas Maduro to American justice, and defend our homeland from dangerous terrorists and cartels—saving American lives.”.

“They will stand behind him in the short term,” said a second senior administration official. And yet, “He is a cost. He’s constantly requiring people to spend political capital on him. The White House is constantly having to come in and save him. The question is, at what point is it too much of a cost to the president?”.

Recent findings suggest that the morning after Hegseth survived the impeachment attempt, he attended a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth was joined at the sacred memorial by his closest aides: Jennifer Hegseth, his third wife and a former Fox News producer who serves as an informal but influential adviser; his chief of staff Ricky Buria, a Marine Corps veteran who followed an unusual path into the top brass; and Tami Radabaugh, another former Fox News producer whom Hegseth hired as a senior adviser.

Recent findings suggest that as the group posed for photos at the Tomb, they chatted and laughed loudly. A US Army sentinel guarding the memorial turned to the group and shouted out a reprimand: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” After video of the moment made for embarrassing headlines, Hegseth awarded the soldier a Joint Service Commendation Medal and posed alongside several Army officers for a photoshoot that was posted on his social media accounts. The Pentagon did not elaborate on why a soldier was awarded a medal for an act as pedestrian as scolding noisy attendees at a memorial. “Hegseth would not have given him that award had the incident not been on TV,” remarked a former senior defense official.

The small group of advisers beside Hegseth has helped the secretary weather a series of scandals in his two years as defense secretary using stage-managed displays of toughness. “He’s a cross between a carnival barker and a personal trainer,” said John Ullyot, who served as chief Pentagon spokesperson and senior adviser to Hegseth until he left the department last year. A loyal Trump backer, Ullyot initially supported Hegseth’s calls to restore standards and excise identity politics from the military. He has since emerged as a fierce public critic and now believes Hegseth should resign.

In his fresh book, The President Deserves Better, Ullyot describes a secretary of defense fixated on self-promotion and content creation. GTA 6 might play best when it hits PC, but it'll be best played with a controller

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I hate to credit Sony's aggressive (and presumably very expensive) marketing campaign for GTA 6—you know, the one which appeared to have also plucked the ability for Xbox to even mention the game by name.
  • We all already know that PC is going to get the best version of GTA 6 when it finally hits our desktops, whenever that might be.
  • In a recent development, I never expected a controller to actively add to my experience, but I also forgot just how many goodies Sony stuffed into this thing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I hate to credit Sony's aggressive (and presumably very expensive) marketing campaign for GTA 6—you know, the one which appeared to have also plucked the ability for Xbox to even mention the game by name. That's something I'm still shocked was even a thing anyone was allowed to do.

So I won't credit it… mostly. We all already know that PC is going to get the best version of GTA 6 when it finally hits our desktops, whenever that might be. But I am going to agree with one part of the whole "Grand Theft Auto 6 plays best on PS5" shtick: the DualSense controller. It's so good that I fear those who reach for a mouse and keyboard will be missing out on some incredible immersion.

In a recent development, I never expected a controller to actively add to my experience, but I also forgot just how many goodies Sony stuffed into this thing. Seriously, Rockstar has taken full advantage of everything the peripheral has to offer.

According to recent reports, I've been weaving through traffic way more in GTA 6 thanks to a huge increase in general vehicle density and some criminally narrow roads that can cause some major bottlenecks. Flooring it all the way from A to B isn't quite as easy as it used to be, which is why I kind of love how you can use the adaptive triggers to comfortably maintain a steady cruising speed before clicking it all the way in as a way to floor it. It makes my speed feel just that little more deliberate, with that tactile feel for when I really want to amp up how fast I'm going.

But driving might actually be the least interesting way Rockstar has made full use of the controller. The parts that have gotten me more than anything are the small ways haptics have been implemented to strengthen story moments or make parts of Leonida feel even more alive.

Industry observers note that the first time I really noticed the controller was back in the beginning of the game, when I'm instructed to go and pick Lucia up from prison. As I'm standing outside as Jason, watching her emerge from the gate, the controller starts thumping just a little bit. A heartbeat. I'm literally feeling Jason's heart racing as Lucia approaches. No dialogue, no internal monologue letting me know how nervous he is. It's such a small detail, but one that massively hammed up the moment for me.

Recent findings suggest that my absolute favourite way it's been implemented, though? The clubs. The goddamn clubs. Leonida's sprawling nightlife is already impressive in isolation—Hitman's Berlin level was the last time I felt this enamoured with a videogame nightclub—but this is where Rockstar went all-in on the controller's haptic feedback. Step into a club and you'll immediately feel the bass pulsating through the controller.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has been revealed that it's not just the same, monorhythmic beat for every song though. The bass perfectly matches the song; those long, teeth-shaking booms cut with shorter, less intense thumps. I feel like I'm back in my first year of university trying to sleep while the nearby student nightclub blasts the same songs until 3am every damn Wednesday, the bass somehow reverberating across the campus and straight through my bedframe.

Industry observers note that when I first set foot inside the Jack of Hearts club at the beginning of Chapter 3, I was practically stunlocked by how much more immersive being able to feel the bass through the controller was making the entire experience. Seriously, I cannot overstate just how much it sucks you into what's happening around you.

Sources indicate that these are all things that I genuinely feel folks are going to miss out on with a simple mouse and keyboard. Sure, your aiming will be better. Yes, none of the things I've described above actually change anything about the gameplay. It'll still be the same GTA 6 no matter what you play with. But for all the ways Rockstar has managed to elevate the experience and the immersion I've been feeling just through something as small as the controller I'm holding? It at least deserves consideration for your go-to playthrough peripheral.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Alabama man is accused of fatally shooting his wife, stepdaughter and her boyfriend in the head as they slept at home.

James Hanks’ wife, Kimberly Hanks, died at a hospital the afternoon of Monday, November 23, after a few days on life support following the attack, the Pike County Sheriff’s Office stated in a news release issued the same day.

James, 64, is facing capital murder charges in the deaths of Kimberly, his stepdaughter, Elizabeth Dean, and her boyfriend, Micheal Catic, per AL.com.

The investigation stems from Thursday, November 19, when a school resource officer alerted deputies that James’ two step-grandchildren hadn’t been picked up from Goshen High School, the sheriff’s office stated in a Friday, November 20, news release.

While trying to find the students’ family members, deputies reached James at his Pike County home and asked whether he knew where his stepdaughter, Dean, and her boyfriend were, according to authorities.

James told deputies Dean and Catic left the home and “didn’t know where they had gone,” according to the sheriff’s office.

Despite James’ claim, cars belonging to Dean and Catic were parked in the driveway outside of the home, indicating they hadn’t left, the agency stated.

Deputies also learned Kimberly never arrived to work that day and noticed her car still parked in the driveway.

Kimberly worked as an ICU nurse at Troy Regional Medical Center, according to a statement the facility shared with WSFA.

Since deputies were unable to contact or locate Kimberly, Dean and Catic, the sheriff’s office decided to enter the home “to determine whether anyone required emergency medical assistance or protection,” the agency mentioned.

While outside the residence, a Pike County Special Response Team first tried to get James to step outside. The team forced their way into the home when James refused to leave and found him in the living room, where they detained him before searching the residence, according to the sheriff’s office.

Authorities ultimately discovered Kimberly, Elizabeth and Catic had been shot in two bedrooms while they appeared to have been asleep.

Dean and Catic were found dead lying in bed together inside one room with gunshot wounds to their head, the sheriff’s office mentioned.

Industry observers note that kimberly was found shot in the head, alive, in bed in another room, according to authorities. She was provided medical care and put on life support ahead of her death.

James’ two stepchildren were placed in the care of other family members as he was taken into custody, according to the sheriff’s office.

A motive for the killings wasn’t specified by law enforcement.

It wasn’t immediately clear whether James had an attorney who could comment on his behalf.

Industry observers note that “We also recognize the emotional toll this tragic incident has taken on the deputies and investigators who have worked tirelessly throughout this investigation,” the agency added. “Incidents like these effect not only the families involved but also the first responders who dedicate themselves to serving our community.”.

"Flood of new AI games" kills retro homebrew competition

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (602 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • "Keeping up with the large number of AI assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI," host James, also known as ZeroPage Homebrew, indicates on the Atari Age forums (thanks, Time Extension).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that creating homebrew games for old consoles and computers is one of retro gaming's proudest traditions, and the Atari Homebrew Awards had been celebrating incredible community creations for the better part of a decade. But now, a wave of games built with AI has killed the ninth annual iteration of the competition as its host tries to figure out what to do.

"Keeping up with the large number of AI assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI," host James, also known as ZeroPage Homebrew, indicates on the Atari Age forums (thanks, Time Extension). "This flood of new AI games forced me reevaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.".

James was "not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I quickly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought.".

It has been revealed that you can probably guess at some of the issues James ran into. He didn't want to allow fully AI-generated games into the competition, but settling on a particular cutoff proved to be impossible. "There is no standard of reporting or calculating how much AI was used in each game," James notes, and even if there were a way to track it all, you'd have to make judgement calls. Is a little AI-generated code okay? Is using AI for testing alright?

"We were always able to come up with a solution for small complications in previous years but the advent of AI marked a seismic shift in the way retro games were being made," James indicates. "I saw no path forward and made the difficult decision to suspend the Atari Homebrew Awards this year. This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year. I know many others feel the same way and I hope to be able to continue this tradition in the coming years as things settle into a latest normal.".

Recent findings suggest that the beauty of retro development scenes for many years is that they were labors of love. Developers were bringing Zelda games to PC and programming all-new Atari 2600 games for little reason other than that they could. But AI code generation has made creating these projects dramatically easier, and fundamentally shifted the vibe of the community, as programmers with minimal skill build buggy, heartless games through Claude prompts. We still haven't figured out what the "new normal" is going to look like.

These are the best retro consoles available today.

His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

#188931. Breaking: Every Version of 'A Christmas Carol,' Ranked (and Where to Stream Them)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Every Version of 'A Christmas Carol,' Ranked (and Where to Stream Them)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2032 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol is the greatest story about Christmas ever written—even better than the one with Mary and Joseph and the manger.
  • I've carefully considered every major theatrical and TV adaptation of A Christmas Carol and rated each in terms of holiday spirit, Dickensian whimsy, and Scrooge-osity to arrive at the definite, no-argument-possible best-to-worst list of Christmas Carols.
  • In a recent development, to rank Christmas Carols, you have to decide what A Christmas Carol is to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol is the greatest story about Christmas ever written—even better than the one with Mary and Joseph and the manger. The 1843 tale of a miser browbeaten by self-righteous ghosts is (probably) the most filmed story of all time. Dozens of cinematic adaptations of A Christmas Carol have been released in theaters and on TV since Scrooge; or Marley's Ghost came out in 1901. Hundreds or thousands if you count re-imaginings and very special episodes of sitcoms. But which version is the very best?

I've carefully considered every major theatrical and TV adaptation of A Christmas Carol and rated each in terms of holiday spirit, Dickensian whimsy, and Scrooge-osity to arrive at the definite, no-argument-possible best-to-worst list of Christmas Carols.

In a recent development, to rank Christmas Carols, you have to decide what A Christmas Carol is to you. My criteria for inclusion: It has to be full-length (at least around an hour long); it has to have been released widely, either in theaters, on network television, or through a larger streaming service, and it has to be fairly close to a direct adaptation—modernizations, re-imaginings, sequels, and that episode of The Six Million Dollar Man don’t count (sorry, Scrooged fans). Using those criteria, I’ve winnowed the Carols down to the 17 you see below, ranked from best to worst, along with where you can stream each one.

Recent findings suggest that it's tough to pick a single adaptation of A Christmas Carol as the absolute best of all time, but the 1984 TV movie version starring George C. Scott is unassailable. Other versions do some things better, but this one does everything right—no mistakes. It stays close to the original text; it's perfectly produced; and it has a consistency of tone and vision that makes it the most balanced of all versions of the story. A Christmas Carol might not have the best Scrooge of all time, but George C. Scott's performance is a solid nine out of ten, and this version features the most adorable and pitiable Tiny Tim of all and the best Ghost of Christmas Present, played by Edward Woodward, who played the policeman in The Wicker Man.

Where to stream it: Roku, Tubi, Pluto TV.

Shot in the midst of the Great Depression, the first sound version of A Christmas Carol digs deeper into the despair and horror of the story than any other adaptation. It’s a bleak, German expressionist Christmas flick, and Seymour Hicks’ sickly, haunted portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge fits the tone perfectly. Instead of delighting in his own crapulence, Hicks plays Scrooge like Satan in The Divine Comedy—he's not the ruler of Hell; he's its most tormented prisoner. Scrooge's miserliness is played as pathology. He wears dirty, torn clothing and shivers miserably while eating gruel because he can’t bring himself to burn a single scrap of coal. Even when he converts, it seems like a manic episode instead of Christmas spirit, suggesting this could be a story about an old man going mad.

Where to stream: Sadly, the version on free streaming services like Tubi and Plex is colorized, but you can watch it on YouTube in glorious black and white.

Industry observers note that this big-budget musical take on the Yuletide classic turns Dickens up to 11. Scrooge is huge, a raucous, crowd-pleasing musical with hundreds of extras, elaborate sets, and a scenery-chewing central performance from Albert Finney to hold it all together. But Finney and tech giant also manage to keep the emotional core of the story intact. The music is great, with memorable tunes like “I Hate People,” a song that Finney snarls instead of sings. Scrooge has the best ghosts of any version of A Christmas Carol, too—you can't beat the cheesy awesomeness of big-money 1970s special effects.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Pluto TV, Plex.

According to recent reports, before Hallmark devoted its corporate life to forgettable holiday-themed romantic comedies, it co-produced one of the best versions of A Christmas Carol ever made. This entire movie belongs to Patrick Stewart, whose nuanced, layered portrayal of Scrooge is the best that has ever been done. His "conversion" scene is so visceral and honest, it brought a tear to my eyes, even though I've seen the exact scene performed in at least 40 other movies, stage plays, and episodes of 1980s sitcoms. Sadly, the paucity of basic cable budgets in the 1990s results in some chintzy-looking sets and laughable special effects that mar an otherwise top-notch production.

Where to stream it: Digital rental only.

It has been revealed that horror director Ti West's Carol adaptation muddies the moral clarity of Dickens' tale and suggests there's something deeply troubling beneath all the Victorian holiday catharsis. With a few exceptions, Ebenezer hits the familiar beats of A Christmas Carol: It delivers the crowd-pleasing rich-jerk-turns-good story moviegoers expect, but West layers in subtle hints along the way that suggest the floorboards are rotten, and if you dance with Christmas joy too hard, you'll fall into the dark basement below. Ebenezer seems to whisper to audiences, "How much does the conversion of one miserly wretch matter in the face of systemic injustice? And isn't he going to snap out of it when the fright wears off anyway?" Bonus: As you'd probably expect from a Ti West movie, the ghosts are genuinely scary.

Where to watch it: In theaters now.

I'm sticking A Muppet Christmas Carol randomly here on the list because you can't reasonably compare it to other versions of the story. The Muppet version is a thing unto itself. Like the Ol' Dirty Bastard, its style has no father. A Muppet Christmas Carol is absolutely delightful from start to finish, for children, grown-ups, cats, dogs, space aliens, and anything else you got. It shouldn't even work to set Michael Caine's serious portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge against a supporting cast of puppets, but somehow it all seems natural.

Recent findings suggest that alastair Sim takes Ebenezer Scrooge on a real journey in this movie. In the first act, he plays Scrooge like Capitalism personified, an uncaring, amoral monument to pure acquisition. He seems like a Scrooge who'd scare away ghosts, but when Marley highlights up dragging his trademark chains, Sim is instantly reduced to pop-eyed fear, like the single chink in his armor is the supernatural. Scrooge then regresses to a childlike, bashful figure as ghosts lead him to different visions, finally emerging from his symbolic death to his rebirth as a Christmas-obsessed guy who lives to serve others. This movie might be among the best of the genre, but an unnecessary subplot about Scrooge's business sandbags the movie through part of the second act.

It has been revealed that mr. Magoo's Christmas Carol was the first animated version of A Christmas Carol and the first animated holiday special ever shown on American TV. The main character, Mr. Magoo, was the star of a one-joke, limited-animation cartoon popular in the early 1960s about an old man who couldn’t see very well, so it’s surprising how carefully crafted and effective this version of A Christmas Carol is. It's weirdly meta too: Jim Backus voices Mr. Magoo, who is a (blind) actor performing as Scrooge in A Christmas Carol on Broadway, so the play is bookended with "this guy can't see!" bits. The songs are strange, memorable and funny (listen to "Razzleberry Dressing" above once and you'll never forget it), but the emotional core of the story remains surprisingly powerful. Jim Backus is amazing.

Where to stream it: Peacock, Roku, Tubi.

I'm breaking my own rule about not including shortened versions of the story because this animated Carol is that great. Its evocative, graceful, hand-drawn look belongs to animation legend Richard Williams and was inspired by the illustrations from the original version of A Christmas Carol. It's a cartoon, but it's not a kiddie cartoon, so the darkness of the ghosts isn't glossed over. Plus, Scrooge is voiced by Alastair Sim, reprising his role from 1951's Scrooge.

Sources indicate that there's nothing wrong with this brightly lit, by-the-numbers take on A Christmas Carol, but it seems designed to appeal to as broad an audience as possible, so the rough edges of the story have been sanded off. The ghosts aren’t that scary. Scrooge isn’t that miserly, etc. It’s fine for a Christmas movie to be lighthearted fun, but the lowered stakes ultimately blunt the emotional resonance of the climax, leading to a mediocre Christmas Carol.

I'm including this version of A Christmas Carol because it's Lifehacker editor Meghan Walbert's favorite. Sorry, Meghan, but this flimsy 1970s TV movie adaptation hasn't aged well. Henry Winkler does a good job as Scrooge, and it's cool to see Burgess Meredith and other old-timey stars, but overall, this is a schmaltzy, plodding film that unwisely replaces a lot of Dickens' best writing with the work of 1970s TV hacks.

Where to stream it: Pluto, Tubi, Amazon Prime.

I really wanted to like Disney’s A Christmas Carol. Robert Zemeckis is a great director and Jim Carrey is a force of nature, but I couldn't get through it. There might be a lot to recommend this version of the story, but using 2009’s technology to create realistic-looking characters was such a puzzling choice. The whole movie looks like a video game cutscene from a PS3 game, and I kept wanting to hit “A” to skip ahead to the gameplay.

It doesn't seem like the producers of this obscure 2012 straight-to-streaming feature had much money to work with, which is too bad. If they had, they might have been able to better realize some of the intriguing ideas behind this movie. It's a straight-up horror take on the tale, but it just isn't scary. Sadly, you can't carry a feature film on good intentions. Overall, a swing and a miss.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Amazon Prime.

The animation in this 1997 musical cartoon version of A Christmas Carol is dated, pedestrian, and ugly. The songs are forgettable, and Scrooge has a pet bulldog for some reason. (The one good joke is that he named his dog "Debit.") It’s just not good, which is a shame, because the cast is overflowing with talent, including Tim Curry as Scrooge, Ed Asner, and Whoopi Goldberg.

Where to stream it: Roku, Pluto TV, Xumo.

Recent findings suggest that this BBC drama goes for a philosophical, moody version of Scrooge, but it doesn’t come together. It’s dark, grim, and so ponderously self-serious that it collapses under its own weight. In an effort to present aspects of A Christmas Carol that haven't been seen before (like "How Marley got his chains"), A Christmas Carol rewrites the original text from the ground up, but it comes across like Dickens' first draft with a bad case of Surf Dracula.

Where to stream it: Hulu, Disney+.

The current state of Dickens adaptation is not good. Netflix's uninspired, sappy, CGI version of A Christmas Carol tries to tart the story up with slapstick, songs, and jokes, but it’s all cynical, lowest-common-denominator horseshit. The dialogue has been dumbed down and joked up. Scrooge has a silly dog for comic relief. They added scatological humor. Think about this: The minds behind Scrooge: A Christmas Carol read Dickens and concluded, “This story would be better with a wacky dog and fart jokes.”.

A Christmas Carol is such a solid story, even a grade-school production of it can be fun to watch. But a cynical production of it is extra terrible, given the message of the story. This terrible ego project is a bottom-of-the-barrel Christmas Carol because it feels like a money grab. Kelsey Grammer sucks as Scrooge, mugging his way through a lightweight performance. Jason Alexander sucks as Marley. Jennifer Love Hewitt is, well, actually pretty good as Scrooge’s Christmas-past romantic interest. She is a rare bright spot in this dreary movie, however. Everything else is mid to terrible. It’s shot and lit like a TV show; the sets are bland and the songs forgettable. Overall, it has the cynical feeling of assembly-line, “let’s get this shit over with” TV production.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Pluto TV, Plex.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a latest trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

According to recent reports, the trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and fresh playable faction.

In a recent development, now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was revealed, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

Sources indicate that in its final few seconds, the trailer shows a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was quickly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively latest addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

Industry observers note that vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

What this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that good afternoon from Washington, where Party Animals has not forgotten the 5 a.m. wake-up required last Tuesday to attend Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s first Pentagon press conference in six months. This was a peculiar one, arranged so Hegseth could brief the public on his own personal battle for career survival.

The briefing kicked off at 8 a.m., but the press had to be at the Pentagon by 6 a.m. for an extensive security screening. I’d like to think that this cruel early start was a consequence of Hegseth’s self-proclaimed sobriety. What kind of drunk drags his sorry carcass before a crowd of jackals before noon? Not any I know.

Sources indicate that but sources I spoke with for a new piece on Hegseth’s war inside the Pentagon told me there was a more Machiavellian motivation for the presser: Donald Trump loves to watch Fox & Friends at 8 a.m. And sure enough, soon after the conclusion of Hegseth’s performance, its intended audience of one offered a review on Truth Social.

Read on for my investigation into Hegseth’s turbulent tenure at the top of the Department of Defense, and what it means for his survival as Democrats take control of Congress in January.

Sources indicate that the reviews are in for Joe Biden’s newly introduced book, Promise Me, America. The Atlantic calls the book “unrepentant.” The New York Times calls it a 400-page “cover letter.” The former president offers the fantastical opinion that he should have stayed in the race in 2024 and faced Trump, quite a position to maintain given he couldn’t voice his own audiobook and limited his press appearances for the release to a soft-focus People magazine story (his publisher did not respond to Party Animals’ multiple requests for an interview). According to the reviews, the former president dedicates scant attention to one of the biggest debacles of his presidency, the war in Gaza, which he abetted thanks to near-unwavering support for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu as 2,000-pound bombs rained down on the densely packed enclave, killing more than 70,000 people. As president, Biden publicly questioned the death toll numbers. “Too many innocent Palestinians were killed,” he now writes, as if possessed by the passive-voice ghost of Donald Rumsfeld. Mistakes were made, indeed. In contrast with his remarkably clinical view of dead Gazans, he writes movingly about his friendship with Netanyahu, recalling his farewell to the prime minister days before leaving the White House: “I still love you, pal.”.

Elon Musk is Sorry About All That.

Just five months ago, Elon Musk was promoting a movie in which a gunman goes on a mass murder rampage targeting supporters of immigration. That this was barely noticed is a sign of just how extreme Musk’s rhetoric has become over the years, as he devolved Xeet by Xeet into the online equivalent of a bum who yells at strangers on the street about race science. Then the midterms happened. After blowing nearly $500 million in an effort to get Republicans elected and falling short in key races, particularly in Texas, the octocentibillionaire seems to be seeking some kind of public rehabilitation. In a virtual appearance at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin that he is “not MAGA”—despite the many photos of Elon wearing a certain conspicuous hat—and that he is actually “a moderate.” Don’t take the hat’s word for it, though, here’s Musk on the record in October 2024: “I’m not just MAGA, I’m Dark MAGA.” Ah, well, nevertheless. He expressed hope for incoming Texas governor Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, and said he felt “foolish” for blowing so many millions to achieve very little. What’s the over/under on how long Moderate Elon will last?

Miller and Marco: The Wall Street Journal has a great report on the close relationship between Stephen Miller and Marco Rubio, who have forged an unlikely alliance despite their past clashes over policy like immigration. It’s a revealing look at how Rubio’s Republican Party lost to Miller’s Republican Party, and how Rubio then jettisoned his entire worldview to join the winning team.

Trump of Wall Street: The Washington Post reports that Trump’s financial disclosure revealed he held between $13 million and $62 million in Nvidia stock as of the end of August. That’s considerably higher than the $615,000 to $1.3 million he held at the end of 2024.

French, Toast: No one should know who “Bo” French is. No one really did until the Republican candidate for Texas Railroad Commission went viral for complaining about a group of college kids celebrating a touchdown at a University of Texas football game. (Some of the kids were not white; French objected to this). He became whatever the opposite of a sensation is and ended up losing his election to a Democrat. Now Politico reports French has taken another blow: River Crest Country Club, the Fort Worth members institution he frequented, has kicked him out.

According to recent reports, garcia’s Hit List: Robert Garcia, the House Democrat who is expected to lead the Oversight Committee in the newly introduced Congress, has begun mapping out his targets. Per The Atlantic: “Garcia this morning sent a dozen letters to high-ranking Trump-administration officials and members of the president’s family, providing the clearest signal yet of which topics—and which people—will likely face the greatest scrutiny once Democrats take control of the House.”.

Oversight O’clock: Latest York Magazine’s Ben Terris went deep on the new era of Democratic oversight, everything from the war with Iran to Trump’s massive beautiful ballroom.

No Longer Satire: Read Joe Bernstein, writing for The Upcoming York Times Magazine, on how America is becoming more and more like Grand Theft Auto.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nearly five years after Boston police officer John O’Keefe died, his teenage niece revealed how she believes his then-girlfriend, Karen Read, was involved in his death.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly five years after Boston police officer John O’Keefe died, his teenage niece revealed how she believes his then-girlfriend, Karen Read, was involved in his death.

While appearing in Netflix’s November docuseries The Trials of Karen Read, O’Keefe’s niece Kayley Furbush explained that she and her younger brother spent several years living with O’Keefe, 46, after their parents died within months of each other.

It has been revealed that “I think Karen knew what had happened, that maybe she had done something to JJ and she didn’t want [it] to almost, like, be a reality,” Furbush said of her uncle’s death. “Or after that, not wanting to believe what she, like, knows is true in her head.”.

After O’Keefe died in January 2022, Read, 46, was arrested for his murder when she was accused of hitting him with her car.

During the high-profile trials, prosecutors argued that Read backed her SUV into O’Keefe and left him in the snow while she was under the influence of alcohol. Meanwhile, Read’s defense claimed he was killed inside of his friend’s house and that she was framed for his murder.

Read’s first trial ended in a mistrial in 2024. She returned to court in 2025 and was eventually acquitted of second-degree murder, manslaughter while operating under the influence and leaving the scene of a collision resulting in death in June of that year.

Despite the major legal victories, Read was found guilty of operating a motor vehicle under the influence of liquor.

Read earned a large group of supporters throughout the trials, all arguing she was innocent.

Furbush also reflected on Read’s celebrity-like status in the docuseries, admitting that she found her behavior upsetting.

“The fact that Karen’s trying to be in the public eye and take pictures with people and, like, smile walking into a murder trial, I’m just disgusted or, like, disturbed by her,” Furbush said while looking back on the trials.

Furbush said Read’s behavior in the spotlight was upsetting because she “treated me like a friend” during her relationship with O’Keefe.

Check our latest news in Google News.

Check our latest news in Apple News.

It has been revealed that “She’s funny. She was always laughing or making us laugh,” Furbush mentioned of her past relationship with Read. “She meshed really well with me and my brother.”.

Despite the media interest in the case, Furbush mentioned she believes people have forgotten about her uncle due to the interest in Read.

“I think people have forgotten about JJ, but I still have hope that something will come from this. For people to understand this wasn’t just some crazy story,” she said. “This was about actual human beings with real emotions. Their jobs, community, close friends — ripped apart because of lies that have been spread.”.

#188926. Why Do AI Posters All Look Like That?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1300 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Why Do AI Posters All Look Like That?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you know “the look” by now.
  • In a recent development, at this point, gone are the days of chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini simply generating text immediately in response to a prompt.
  • According to recent reports, to borrow a classic and implausible example, if you were to give an AI chatbot the instruction “Make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich,” it would start by generating step-by-step instructions on how to make the sandwich before trying to make one (if it could).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you know “the look” by now. Every poster for a business or event has pictures of uncanny-looking people, buildings that don’t look right, and always that one font. But why? If generative AI is supposedly able to “think” and be “creative,” why do so many of its results come out looking exactly the same? The answer is complicated, and it has to do with what chatbots define as “thinking.”.

In a recent development, at this point, gone are the days of chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini simply generating text immediately in response to a prompt. Some very fast models do, but most employ what’s known as “thinking models”, which are a bit of a misnomer. The “thinking” really just consists of generating a set of sub-prompts before executing the main one. And it’s in that hidden, generated text that most of the “choices” (to the extent that we can call the statistical output of an AI model a “choice”) occur that determine how a design looks.

According to recent reports, to borrow a classic and implausible example, if you were to give an AI chatbot the instruction “Make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich,” it would start by generating step-by-step instructions on how to make the sandwich before trying to make one (if it could). Most of this happens invisibly in the background, and many proprietary chatbots won’t show you their in-process “thinking” prompts even if you ask.

In the case of an AI poster, it might break down “make a poster” into smaller steps such as “create a design brief for a poster.” To demonstrate this while doing some testing for this piece, I added additional prompts for ChatGPT to explain the “design briefs” it generated, which included details like layout, colors, and typography.

Recent findings suggest that the problem is those instructions are still subject to the same flaws as any other AI-generated text. They can’t properly fact-check; they can’t walk into the real world and see the thing they’re describing; and they can hallucinate or fall back on stale formats that become easy to notice after a while.

Sources indicate that for example, while testing, I had ChatGPT generate a poster for a Lifehacker-themed nightclub. In every case, the underlying brief it generated outlined some basic details, but occasionally it added things I hadn’t asked for. This included additional text, iconography, and in one case it even added the “design brief” explanation I had requested as the bottom half of the poster.

Those mistakes filter into the final product, when the brief is then fed into the image generator that ultimately makes the poster. In my case, ChatGPT indicated me the underlying explanations for its reasoning (though even that could be different from what was actually sent to the image generator), but most people who use a chatbot for this task won’t see these factors before getting the final result.

While most chatbots won’t show you exactly what underlying “thinking” they use, most can be coaxed into describing the vague outlines of how they reached certain outcomes. And those descriptions provide some insight into why certain chatbots keep outputting similar results over and over. It doesn’t take long for some patterns to emerge. For example, any prompt to generate a poster for a nightclub almost invariably generated a brief that had specifications for a color palette including “electric purple,” “electric yellow,” and “electric pink.”.

Industry observers note that the reason for this should be pretty obvious: When the statistical model underlying LLMs needs to come up with an example for “colors for a nightclub poster,” the most obvious answers are neon, high-energy colors. Unless you know something about the specific club’s vibe (and write that out and feed it to the chatbot), the AI will have to fill in the gaps with something. And that something will be based on the same statistics it uses to predict any word.

This pattern of repetition was everywhere in all the design rationale ChatGPT gave me. Across multiple attempts to generate a Club Lifehacker poster, the generated design brief added an overarching “concept” that described the fictional club’s atmosphere as “high-energy” and “futuristic.” Every bot mentioned using images with the “silhouette” of either the DJ or a dancing crowd (often both). All the text had to be “bold” and “futuristic.".

It has been revealed that if there's one dead giveaway that a poster was made with AI, it's that one brush-stroke font that they all seem to use. Now, this is a bit more speculative, but I have a theory on where that specific design comes from. And it’s worth noting upfront that this seems to only apply to posters generated by ChatGPT specifically.

One of the most common factors I found in my design brief testing was the use of phrases like “brush lettering” or “brush script.” Brush lettering is a design term that refers to using any number of methods like markers, paint brushes, or brush pens to write text. In digital design, that can take the form of fonts that are designed to emulate the look of fancy, handwritten text.

Industry observers note that in every test poster I created, however, ChatGPT seemed to take the phrase “brush lettering” rather literally. Every instance I encountered of a design brief that mentioned any kind of “brush” text generated an image with letters that looked as though they were created with a broad paint brush. A human designer would understand “brush lettering” to mean “something that looks handwritten," but ChatGPT didn’t seem capable of understanding the phrase as anything other than using an actual paint brush.

Sources indicate that the generated posters aren’t even using a “font,” strictly speaking. (Often, letters that should be identical had slight variations.) The image generator part of the chatbot is still a diffusion model, so it can’t employ a vector-based font, per se. But the brush-style font is so common that its look surfaces in any statistical model.

According to recent reports, this is an odd quirk of ChatGPT specifically, and it’s possible that it could change in the future. Especially if OpenAI intentionally tries to train this behavior out of its chatbot. However, it’s helpful to illustrate the underlying mechanism. The only way a chatbot can conceptualize design elements in a visual medium is to generate more specific text to feed to the image generator. And that text is just as prone to mistakes and blandness as any other AI model.

Sources indicate that I’ve been examining this with a focus on the kinds of posters ChatGPT generates because they’re very common, but posters (or any AI-generated content) from other models might look different. Every model has its own tendencies. For example, a lot of vibecoded websites are made with Anthropic’s Claude, and you can often tell by the tiny text, buttons with rounded corners, and tile-based layouts.

In a recent development, to a certain extent, this is inevitable. While AI models are very different from humans and do not make “choices” in the same way people do, design elements still have to come from somewhere, and whether human or AI, it’s impossible to make these decisions in a vacuum. Humans will have preferences based on the things they like or emotionally resonate with, and AI models will have tendencies based on what their statistical model determines is the most appropriate output.

That means that an AI model’s “style” is naturally going to change over time. Even if a model improves or makes fewer mistakes, it’s impossible to ever change the fact that all ChatGPT images are made by ChatGPT. Whatever you generate with any particular model will have a lot in common with what everyone else who uses the same tool generates.

God of War Laufey's Faye actor jumps from games to live-action, as Amazon casts Deborah Ann Woll in upcoming series

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.
  • Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series.
  • Sources indicate that amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first revealed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Sources indicate that amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

Recent findings suggest that there's no release date yet for the show, but it's mentioned to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

Sources indicate that "We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica mentioned at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon.".

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back, too.

According to recent reports, "Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll mentioned of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad.".

All GTA 6 Kitty Litter lab locations

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that taking Out Kitty Litter's lab locations in GTA 6 is a mission in Tyrone's questline, and sees you searching the city for 18 secret labs (after the first one he directs you to).
  • Sources indicate that it'll take a little while, but it's well worth it to get the unique gold SMG at the end.
  • Last note: if you want to unlock map markers for the labs yourself versus relying on these videos, you can threaten cooks in certain labs to potentially reveal them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that taking Out Kitty Litter's lab locations in GTA 6 is a mission in Tyrone's questline, and sees you searching the city for 18 secret labs (after the first one he directs you to). Every lab has a red smoking chimney and a blue and white Spin On This laundry van parked outside.

Sources indicate that it'll take a little while, but it's well worth it to get the unique gold SMG at the end. Plus, Tyrone will start buying narcotics from you for the highest price possible. To destroy each lab, simply shoot a smoking pink flask and then run away. I've also laid these out in the most optimal order, separated into regions, so you're not driving back and forth across Vice City.

Last note: if you want to unlock map markers for the labs yourself versus relying on these videos, you can threaten cooks in certain labs to potentially reveal them.

In a recent development, after you complete some missions for Tyrone (when you meet him with Dre'Quan during Dealer's Choice) he'll direct you to this trailer park in La Perle where you destroy the first Kitty Litter lab and start the hunt for the others. You can see the route to the lab in the video above.

Sources indicate that you can find this one in the trailer park opposite Zenon's Pawn Shop Ammu-Nation in La Perle. As soon as you go through the main gate, you can see the trailer with the funnel chimney where they're cooking straight ahead. Sneak around the back and break inside to find the lab. Or take out the three guys in front and go in that way.

Just across the road from the Mezzasega Espresso and Slinger in the Decor District. Pull off to the right of the road into the Williams + Whitaker Homeware and Decor car park. You'll see a garage with a shutter at the far end with a smoking chimney and the laundry van parked. Open the shutter to find a lone guy in the lab.

This one is behind Peterson's Autoshop in Rockridge, directly south across the road from the Blessed Food Market, under the overpass, on the border between Rockridge and La Perle. Head through the main yard and turn left to spot the laundry van. Break into it, move it forward, and open the shutter behind to find the lab.

Just east of Fleeca Field stadium, next door to Xero Gas - Rockridge. You'll spot the blue and white laundry van parked off to the side of the road behind a wall. Head down that alley and turn right to find a garage door you can open with the lab inside.

On the east side of the condominium building directly south of the Vice City Hospital, by Emilio's Auto Center Gas. Look for the closed road with the laundry van parked at the southern end and some staircases and flats off to the side with the chimney spewing smoke. The lab is through the white door on the bottom floor.

Just down the road to the west of Bump and Grind coffee and Salon Belle, in a block of flats southeast of Fleeca Fields stadium. You can see the laundry van parked outside. The lab is on the upper floor on the left side in apartment 5, where you can see the smoking chimney. Break in via the front door to find the lab.

Industry observers note that this lab is an easy one to find, around the back of Cross My Heart Tattoos. Head around the right side, turn left, and look to your left for the garage door with the guy sitting down guarding it, with the lab inside.

This lab is in the block of flats to the southeast of the Jack of Hearts and Urban Legendz, with the laundry van parked out front. Look inside apartment 103 on the first floor on the left side. It's quite hard to get away from this lab blowing up, so shoot it from outside and run away. Also this will likely cause a big shootout in the block, so book it.

This lab is to the southwest of your apartment in Chapter 3 and to the east of the Crosstown Mule - City Line marker. Look for an overgrown lot with the laundry van parked in it. The garage with the lab is just behind that.

This lab is directly west of Down Town Pawn, just between Rideout Customs and the Vargo's Gas station. Just past the gas station, look to the left where its fuel sign is to spot a laundry van, and further down the track, the garage with the lab and smoking chimney above it.

This lab is close to Xero Gas - Tequesta and west of Vice Seven Condominiums gym. When driving east to west past the station, turn right and keep an eye on your right towards the two floored condominiums for the laundry van parked outside. You want the set of staircases to the right of the van. Take the right side one up to the first floor to find the lab door directly ahead.

Industry observers note that this lab is in a trailer park directly east down the road from Arrow Gas - VCIA, also west under the bridge from Pawn City and Vice City Firearms. Turn into the trailer park, take the first right and drive a little way around the corner to spot the trailer with the smoking chimney on the left. You can enter via a window around the other side to find the lab.

Industry observers note that this lab is located in the far south of Salton, north of the Pay 'N' Spray - Salton, next door to the Slator Towing Inc robbery. Go around the south side of the derelict block of flats and climb the dumpster to jump up through the open window to find the lab.

This lab is west down the road from Xero Gas - Salton. Cross the train tracks, then keep an eye on your right for a carpark with a blue and white laundry van, then turn right into it to spot the building with the smoking chimney on the right. Hop the fence straight ahead and turn right to find one guy guarding the garage with the lab.

This lab is easy to find, directly south of Salon Perez and Safia Restaurant in Little Cuba. Look for some bungalows on the left with the laundry van parked outside. It's in the building with the chimney to the left of the one the van is parked in front of. The lab is the second door along.

This lab is north up the road from the Pay 'N' Spray - Balsero. Turn left down the alley with the laundry van parked to find a guy guarding the gate, a couple of guys inside, and the lab in an open garage further back behind them.

This lab is in a trailer park southeast from the Balasero jewelry stores, across the river. If driving from the east and the city, turn left before the bridge, turn right, then turn left and head a little way down to spot the trailer with the funnel chimney and laundry van outside. Sneak around back to get in and find the lab.

In a recent development, this lab is south across the river from Ron's Car Wash and Gas. Head over the bridge, across the junction, then keep an eye out to your left to spot where the laundry van is parked. The lab is just in the building beyond the gate with the smoking chimney. The door requires a code which is 1999 (referencing the billboard up to the right).

There are three main advantages to destroying all the Kitty Litter labs and completing the Spin On This mission with Tyrone and those are:.

Recent findings suggest that you'll also get $2,000 a lab, plus $10,000 for the Spin On This mission, meaning $48,000 altogether. Since I did everything, it's unclear to me whether these rewards are for destroying every lab, or the mission specifically that you get after you destroy 15 of them. Either way, if you want all of this, destroy all the labs in the city and complete the mission.

  • The easter egg results in your proud ownership of Tommy Vercetti's iconic Hawaiian button-up from GTA: Vice City, but much, much more importantly, it opens up a literal portal to the '1980s setting and 2002 graphics of GTA: Vice City, but instead of Tommy, you're still inhabiting the very confused body of Jason from GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I felt like I had stumbled upon a real-life cryptid when I found Bigfoot hanging around in GTA 6, but it turns out that's actually one of the more easily findable Easter eggs of probably hundreds that won't be discovered for months if not years. There's a viral video going around showcasing an incredibly elaborate Easter egg that I'm convinced would've remained a secret for a long, long while if it weren't for someone with an encyclopedic knowledge of GTA: Vice City and its many cheat codes.

Recent findings suggest that that person is a content creator who goes by Memeio, who says they are "the first person to ever crack this code in the world," and I believe them. But before we get into it, here's your spoiler warning in case you want to try finding this one on your own at some point, although that seems unlikely.

The easter egg results in your proud ownership of Tommy Vercetti's iconic Hawaiian button-up from GTA: Vice City, but much, much more importantly, it opens up a literal portal to the '1980s setting and 2002 graphics of GTA: Vice City, but instead of Tommy, you're still inhabiting the very confused body of Jason from GTA 6. It's a hell of a mind trip to see, and I can only imagine it would be even more surreal to experience in the game.

As Memeio explains in the below video, the actual process of unlocking this Easter egg involves pressing various buttons and pulling various levers in a precise order at different substations across the map, but finding out the right order of everything took "literally 3 days of rotting and searching for power stations.".

I discovered this GTA 6 easter egg about 3 days ago, here it is in video form, I think I'm the first person to ever crack this code in the world so enjoy! #GTA6 https://t.co/vTORjUlYNiNovember 23, 2026.

It has been revealed that memeio was first clued in by an extremely subtle auditory cue that Memeio says is "a sound effect from Vice City," which apparently plays when you power up the radio tower in Key Lento. From there, individual letters appearing on the exteriors of substations spelled out a phrase from GTA: Vice City that correlates with a cheat code, which Memeio translated to an order by which to press the levers at all 12 substations. How they came up with this, no one knows, but it is really frikkin' cool.

Recent findings suggest that seeing stuff like this makes me wonder what bigger, even more complicated easter eggs might be hiding in GTA, and then I get kind of sad because I know I'll never have the patience to find them on my own. Cheers to people like Memeio.
